Nossos caminhos se cruzam novamente, separadas pelo tempo. O objetivo dela é o meu, e minha cicatriz é a dela. Confio que minha jornada não acabará quando eu entrar naquele receptáculo... São muitas aventuras por vir, afinal!

Valory

4081.title: A Mensagem do Céu
4081.text:
Foi escrito pelos Antigos. Seu chamado estranho e melódico ultrapassa o vazio ensurdecedor e atrai os dignos e justos. Não consigo ler. Vejo tudo embaçado... Temo que essa mensagem não seja para mim. Tento estudá-la, entendê-la... Mas quanto mais aprendo, mais entendo que conheço poucas coisas. 

Posso observar a Cidade Submersa daqui, mas não tive muita paz. Recentemente, alguém atrapalhou minha pesquisa com um assobio agonizante. A princípio, achei que fosse um sanguinário, mas felizmente me enganei. Talvez eles aprendam o significado da mensagem da estrela.

Para todos que seguiram o chamado: peguem minhas flechas e deixe que elas guiem vocês.

4082.title: Uma Emboscada Repentina
4082.text:
Avançamos pela lama, caules e pântanos até alcançar uma clareira. Além dela, o piche virava água, e o junco cedia espaço para bambus e palmeiras.

Me abaixei para lavar minhas mãos em uma lagoa cercada de lírios-de-um-dia, que se estendia em direção a vinhas e tocos cobertos de musgo mais à frente. Suas cores vibrantes e cheiro me lembraram do meu amor. Talvez esse momento de descuido indicasse o meu fim.

Uma família de sapos saiu do mato, cada um mais assustado que o outro. Olhei para cima e dei de cara com a ponta de uma lança que saía do mato escuro com o reflexo rompido na água.
Os rumores eram verdade. Os Draks tinham voltado... e, nesse momento, eu estava diante de sua sede de sangue.

Enquanto eu segurava a respiração, o Drak com a lança deixou seus olhos vagarem. Quando cruzou o olhar com os Ancestrais ao redor, ele corrigiu a postura, gritou e soltou a arma. Seu corpo se recolheu em uma postura de oração, afundando os joelhos no chão à minha frente. Me afastei pegando uma pedra afiada para usar como proteção improvisada enquanto tropeçava... Não havia necessidade, já que as feras veneram meus companheiros de viagem como mensageiros de seus deuses e guardiões dos portões de Ark Morgo, sua terra dos mortos.

Como esse equívoco surgiu, não sei dizer. Mas hoje, ele me salvou de parar em Ark Morgo. Se eu estivesse sozinha, não teria essa sorte.

— Rainha Jezmina de Orindell

4083.title: Velhas Feridas Reabertas
4083.text:
Nós entramos na Santuário Noturno da humanidade, atravessamos seu limiar com facilidade e alegria, compartilhando nossas vozes e conhecimento.

Apesar disso, enquanto os brutais Drak construíam seus templos com ossos quebrados, suas oferendas não nos interessavam, e por isso não olhamos para eles.

Uma farsa, um fracasso, um mau passo fatídico, pois as criaturas viram isso como um desafio, uma honra a ser conquistada em batalha. Quando atacaram a humanidade para chamar nossa atenção, nós recuamos... e juramos nunca mais escolher um lado, mesmo quando a Mortalha surgiu.

4084.title: O Feitiço Que Me Traiu
4084.text: Não acredito! Finalmente criei um feitiço de cura! Mas... ele cura os outros?! Dá para acreditar? O que vou fazer com isso? Não me interessa que os outros vivam mais... Pelo menos estou no caminho certo. A próxima tumba me espera. Ouvi dizer que alguns jovens ousaram atravessá-la, desafiando seus obstáculos. Quem chegasse no outro lado... bem, viveria. Deve ficar perto de Fenda Minerada, em direção a Lodo Preto.

4085.title: Criatividade do Mineiro
4085.text:
Eu tenho trabalhado na mina desta região todos os dias, mas ultimamente não consigo parar de pensar que talvez seja possível fazer mais com esses cristais de água-marinha do que apenas tirá-los da pedra. Eu triturei um pouco deles com um moedor pequeno e produzi o pó mais fino e brilhante que já vi.

Depois de misturá-lo com alguns ingredientes que tinha em casa, acho que criei o pigmento perfeito. Amanhã, vou preparar um lote pequeno e mostrá-lo ao Casper.

Talvez essa seja a minha chance de sair da mina para sempre. Pode ser o começo de algo muito maior.

4086.title: Reconstrução
4086.text:
Os Drak'Dal se afastaram por tempo demais. 

Todos os nossos templos viraram pó! 
Os Drak'Dal vão mostrar aos Ancestrais a verdadeira força! Que os Ancestrais cometeram um erro com humanos carnudos! Os Drak'Dal não vão construir na sombra de ninguém! 

Construam um novo lar! Construam para Dalszul! Construam, ou a Mãe da Ninhada Vesztah arrancará suas cabeças!

Rá Rá!

4087.title: Sem Lírios-de-um-dia
4087.text:
Precisamos de mais lírios-de-um-dia para as lâmpadas do berçário de filhotes de Drak.
Somente um brilho fogoso faz os filhotes de Drak quererem sair do ovo.

Tha'Riel me disse que filhotes de Drak pensam que é o sol no horizonte.
Espero que todos nasçam logo, antes que Kra'Thul venha e quebre os ovos.

Banho de sangue terrível, muita faxina.

4090.title: O que deixo para trás
4090.text:
Em meus dias finais, sinto a pressão do fardo que meus parentes colocaram sobre meus ombros. Percebo agora que foi tolice tentar manter a união familiar. Dos meus 7 filhos, nenhum veio ao meu leito de morte... então declaro que nenhum deles vai aproveitar os frutos do meu esforço!

Quero que meu bem mais precioso, uma obra de arte, seja herdada pelos meus filhos. No entanto, a peça será destruída e dividida em 8 partes. Essas partes serão distribuídas entre meus 7 filhos, inutilizando a obra outrora inestimável.
Por fim, quero ser enterrado com a última parte, no topo da colina perto da base do forte. Que a terra me abrace como meus filhos nunca fizeram.

4091.title: Carta de Recomendação, Dia 45 do Ocaso do Ano, 497 E.A.
4091.text:
Instituto CROMWELL de Defesa Imperial
Memorando para General Rasmus

Carta de Recomendação para C-25-1019-DA (DARYA ARKANOV).

É com grande prazer que recomendo a aluna D. ARKANOV para a próxima expedição às Portas Noturnas no fronte dos Picos Albaneve.
Ela provou sua lealdade e suas habilidades de liderança em diversas excursões, e foi a primeira da turma em "História Imperial" e "Antigos: Anatomia dos Adversários". 
Ela até expressou interesse na magia arcana dos Antigos fora da sala de aula. Os desvios doutrinários (tolerados) dela podem ser úteis em sua pesquisa.

Portanto, acreditamos que D. ARKANOV será uma boa adição à sua equipe. Continuamos disponíveis para quaisquer perguntas ou solicitações. 

Bendito seja o Senhor Vorgoth, Guarda do Norte e Governante de Rimgard!
J. Lincoln, Diretor

4092.title: O Berço da Montanha
4092.text:
As montanhas são seu berço, os ventos te fazem dormir
O Pico Uivante é seu ventre, a torta você deve ingerir

Um ovo vai chocar e ir atrás de quem não quer comer
Termine o que seus pais fizeram, ou o petisco será você

Um uivo desesperado vai clamar por ti, os ecos sabem seu nome,
Então apresse-se e limpe o prato, ou a morte te consumirá

4093.title: Isso Não Vai Acabar Bem
4093.text:
Desde que começamos a construir este Poço de Elixir, o chão não para de tremer. 

A neve ficou cinzenta. Ecos sussurram palavras que nunca foram ditas em voz alta. Podemos ouvir algo dentro da montanha.

Acho que estamos corrompendo algo que nem entendemos ainda. Seja o que for, não quero estar por perto quando despertar... Só espero que os postos avançados terminem logo suas balistas.

4094.title: Desejo profundo
4094.text:
Nunca vi algo tão sombrio, mas tão fascinante. É como se estivessem sussurrando, implorando para que eu os tome para mim. Preciso pegar os Blocos de Obsidiana, é um desejo que não consigo ignorar. 
Mas onde guardá-los em segurança? Talvez acima das poças de lava... Quem se arriscaria a ir até lá? Só um tolo. 

Não sei se conseguirei, mas esses blocos certamente me levarão para o caminho da escuridão... Pelo menos terei o que desejo.

4095.title: Maior que a Vida!
4095.text:
Esse templo escondido é uma beleza! Essa sala é sinistra e empoeirada, mas essa entrada é o que mais me intriga...

Será que os Antigos produziram essas portas incrivelmente gigantescas para a raça deles? Ou será que elas surgiram antes dos Antigos...? Será que as pessoas que viviam aqui milênios atrás eram... muito altas ou algo assim?Pessoas altas são superestimadas. Adoraria ter um rei corpulento e baixo. Com um porte físico desses, eles se encaixariam perfeitamente em nossa família.

Deve haver muitos outros templos! O que será que vou encontrar? Estou cansada das minhas viagens, mas uma aventura a mais não fará mal!

– Braelyn

4096.title: Pontes e Laços Quebrados
4096.text:
A luz dos Ancestrais não trouxe a cegueira, mas a visão. Enquanto o branco nos envolvia, seus raios caleidoscópicos desceram e me colocaram em um sono profundo. E lá, tive um sonho.

Eu estava nas terras do meu irmão, em uma época antes da corrupção. Campos exuberantes, aninhados em um vale beijado pelo litoral. Do oceano, veio um chamado. Era um sinal. Devemos colocar Receptáculos da Chama além do nosso litoral a qualquer custo.
Depois de comunicar minha visão aos Ancestrais, descobri que as palavras eram inúteis. Eles já sabiam para onde deveríamos ir. E então fomos, com tênues rastros de luz ainda dançando entre as estrelas.

Esta ponte fica no caminho mais rápido para a Bacia das Águas do Véu, mas está avariada. Meus colegas viajantes acham que é possível seguir para o leste e contornar a borda da mata até chegarmos ao mar. Tremo só de pensar.

A esta altura, meu irmão, o Senhor Vorgoth, já deve ter partido para as Ilhas elevadas... o lar dos Ancestrais. Apesar disso, tenho medo de vê-lo. Atrás de um arbusto, na sombra distorcida de uma folha de Monstera, no meu próprio reflexo ao mergulhar em um lago, em meu sono mais profundo...

Eu e ele somos do mesmo sangue. Às vezes, temo que sejamos mais próximos do que eu gostaria.
Rezo para que meu sonho não se transforme em um pesadelo.

— Rainha Jezmina de Orindell

4097.title: Um Refúgio Final
4097.text:
É isso.
O último refúgio de Lodo Preto. Uma cidade submersa protegida por pântanos e espinheiros.
Quem vier aqui descansará atrás de um portão mágico que só pode ser aberto por botões escondidos no matagal.

Olhar para essas paredes desmoronando me enche de fascínio... e medo. As memórias desta cidade se perderam no tempo, eternamente adormecidas debaixo do piche. Acrescentei por engano algumas lembranças minhas a este covil de tesouros escondidos... não apenas deixei minhas pegadas na lama, mas também minhas botas! Vou deixá-las para trás... Minhas roupas pesam com recordações e imundície.

Isso me faz pensar... será que a humanidade foi esquecida assim como as histórias daqui foram enterradas? E se acontecer, se racharmos, desmoronarmos e desaparecermos como os ossos abaixo... poderemos nos redescobrir e reconstruir? Só quem for Porta-Chama saberá. 

Espero poder lhe ajudar a construir o seu futuro. Esculpir o caminho que você trilhará, elevar e aparar sua queda... Espero que minhas palavras alcancem você, mesmo a constelações de distância, um eco atravessando o tempo. 

Acredito em você, Porta-Chama.
E um dia, espero poder agradecer.

— Rainha Jezmina de Orindell, 509 E.A.

4098.title: Nascimento dos Novos Deuses — Fyraszh
4098.text:
Quando ouviu a lenda de Merphisz, Fyraszh irrompeu da multidão de filhotes de Drak. 

"Por que se debater na água pela eternidade? Por que se ajustar ao capricho das ondas quando se pode forjar o próprio caminho no fogo?" Ele perguntou, vermelho com tanta fúria. Cheio de determinação para superar seu irmão, Fyraszh viajou não em distância, mas em profundeza. Ele partiu para tomar o núcleo da montanha, para forjar sua glória em metal derretido e calor líquido. 

Quando os outros voltaram a vê-lo, suas escamas haviam se endurecido como carvão, e a pele sob elas brilhava como o sol. Adornado com cinzas e ouro, ele gritou do topo da montanha: "Viram? A montanha ruge e cospe, entoando nosso nome e o de nosso clã! Drak'Fyr! Drak'Fyr!"

E conforme a montanha realmente cuspia e rugia, uma fonte tão brilhante quanto o sol poente irrompeu atrás ele. O brilho âmbar engoliu seu corpo, mas elevou sua alma até Ark Mongo, onde seria líder por toda a eternidade.

4099.title: Magia de Gelo
4099.text:
Sempre levei jeito com magia, mas abandonei esse caminho há muitos anos.
Quando eu era jovem, costumava ficar perto do Lagoa da Rendeira, no nordeste. O frio forte não me incomodava, de tanto que eu me concentrava no espetáculo que ocorria sempre que os feiticeiros vinham treinar.
Com um movimento do pulso, eles faziam cristais de gelo flutuarem e enfeitavam o lago congelado com uma teia de fissuras delicadas.

Em uma noite, um praticante que não reconheci se empolgou demais ao lançar um feitiço e tropeçou. Um principiante, imagino, iluminando o céu do norte em um momento e afundando na água em seguida.
Fiquei na beira do lago, esperando ele voltar, mas seu equipamento de feitiçaria encharcado o afundava cada vez mais. Se a noite fria não tivesse me obrigado a ir embora, ainda eu ainda estaria esperando.

Foi assim que escolhi uma vida tranquila em volta de uma fogueira quentinha, em vez das profundezas de um lago congelante.

4100.title: Barbatanas ou Bravatas?
4100.text:
No meu tempo, eu era um rapaz bagunceiro. Eu passava cada dia de aula na praia em vez de sentado na carteira da escola, chutando castelos de areia de estranhos e jogando pedrinhas na água.

Uma vez, vi um pequeno barco ao longe, com uma figura sombria se balançando nele. Enquanto eu focava minha atenção para lá, essas formas se misturavam em uma só, perturbando a água ao redor. Alguém tinha caído no lago? Esperei para ver a pessoa sair da água, mas ninguém apareceu.

Momentos depois, uma criatura feita de algas marinhas e água salgada se ergueu entre as ondas que arrebentavam na praia. Estava bem mais próxima que o barco, e conforme se aproximava, comecei a enxergar um rosto envelhecido sob o monte de algas. Era o capitão.

Perguntei como ele havia conseguido atravessar as águas entre o barco afundado e a praia tão rapidamente. Ele sorriu e disse: "O beijo de uma sereia me deu nadadeiras, garoto!" e saiu dali em uma corrida lenta.

Só depois que notei que os pés dele tinham deixado pegadas estranhas na areia. Será que a história ele era mesmo verdade?

4101.title: Visitantes Bêbados e Pagamentos Estranhos
4101.text:
Um cliente estranho veio aqui hoje. 

Um homem bruto, alto e calado. Algum tipo de cavaleiro ou mercenário... Nunca vi aquela insígnia. Ele claramente já havia bebido muito vinho, ou grogue.
Ele não tinha ouro, então tentei expulsá-lo, mas foi em vão. Ele continuou resmungando, com os olhos bem abertos e apontando para o rum na prateleira de cima com a mão que estava quase pesada demais para levantar.

Seus braços caíam sobre o balcão no meio de seus gestos, como se seu corpo não conseguisse acompanhar as demandas, ou como se seus membros fossem feitos de sacos de grão molhados.
Irritado por sua própria fraqueza e falta de bebida, ele arrancou suas manoplas e as jogou no outro lado do cômodo rosnando. 
Fui para baixo do bar. Quando vi sua mão se estender para baixo do balcão, pensei que ele me atacaria... Em vez disso, ele tropeçou e foi até o gabinete de bebidas.
Ele levou a garrafa à boca e saiu. 

Suas manoplas foram tudo que ele deixou para trás. Elas parecem valiosas, então as guardei no sótão por enquanto, para o caso de ele voltar com menos álcool na mente e mais ouro no bolso.

4102.title: Duas Vezes no Mesmo Lugar
4102.text:
Quando uma tempestade se forma, sinto as nuvens sobre aquela ruína de Drak'Dal aqui perto... Um fenômeno estranho. É como se a chuva e o trovão fossem atraídos para lá, por magnetismo ou magia.

Sempre achei que um raio nunca cairia no mesmo lugar, mas talvez eu esteja errado.

Parece que os raios acertam os velhos pilares com mais frequência. Será que aquele casebre encoberto tem algum artefato interessante? Ou apenas fica no meio de um vale sem motivo? Quem sabe...?

4103.title: O Peso do Tempo
4103.text:
Agora estou velho demais... até cuidar das bananeiras já ficou difícil. Eu sonhava em reformar nossa casa e dar uma nova vida a ela, mas não tenho força para isso.

Os blocos de construção para consertar o nosso telhado ainda estão no sótão, juntando poeira. Acho que vão ficar lá para sempre, intocados, assim como os planos que eu tinha.

E ainda assim... minha esposa está orgulhosa de tudo o que eu já fiz. Isso me conforta. Talvez isso seja suficiente. Eu sou suficiente.

4104.title: Lenda da Estrela Cadente
4104.text:
Séculos atrás, o nosso reino era árido. Desertos intermináveis se espalhavam por todas as direções, e os céus ficaram cobertos de um alcatrão preto e pesado.

E então, o céu se rachou no meio para revelar um mar cintilante. Uma inundação de estrelas cadentes brotou, deixando rastros de cores e ventos à medida que pintavam o horizonte.
Com o impacto, elas pressionaram o solo, separando-o. Pouco depois, nossos ventos foram marcados por montanhas, vales e água. Mas nem todas as estrelas geraram vida. Algumas tentaram levá-la.

Duas espadas caíram das alturas, uma inferior e outra superior, e elas atingiram o topo dos nossos alabastros. Uma delas adormeceu debaixo da neve fresca e das flores de genciana, a outra foi engolida pela boca de uma caverna nas alturas.

Seriam elas maus presságios? Relíquias de um duelo do espaço infinito? Um presente dos ancestrais? Talvez nunca saibamos.

4105.title: Nestes cumes varridos pelo vento
4105.text:
Nos sentamos entre os penhascos e pontas de lâminas, abençoados pela neve pura. Para buscar compreensão, para recuperar a unidade que nossa espécie perdeu na névoa.

Que terra vasta e uivante. Que eco silencioso, impotente e estilhaçado. Nossas mentes estão congeladas, incapazes de entender razão ou compaixão. Estamos divididos como vales, rodeados por penhascos de marfim que nos perfuram, distorcem nossas existências e forçam nossas ações.

Alguns de nós se erguerão. Alguns permanecerão. O mais velho será puro, o mais jovem perdido e moldado em novas formas.
Já não somos um. Somos chamas gêmeas dançando ao ritmo de melodias diferentes.

4108.title: Decreto Real
4108.text:
Em nome da sua alteza, Senhor Vorgoth, Guarda do Norte e Governante de Rimgard
Sua Senhoria declara por meio deste uma ordem executiva:

Todas as unidades designadas ao Programa de Expansão devem parar de se referir ao Senhor Vorgoth de formas desagradáveis e criativamente indecentes.

Todas as unidades designadas ao Programa de Expansão devem relatar casos de fofocas e reclamações banais para que possam ser levados à justiça, sujeitos à máscara de tortura ou, no caso de ofensas repetitivas, a uma visita às masmorras pelo tempo que o supervisor julgar necessário.
Punições adicionais, impostas de forma mais adequada com uma lança de madeira afiada, de diâmetro e comprimento específicos, poderão ser executadas à vontade. —

(O resto do decreto está muito desgastado e rasgado para decifrar.)

4109.title: Você viu o mensageiro real?
4109.text:
Deveríamos ter recebido o mensageiro duas noites atrás, mas ele ainda não chegou. 
Ainda estamos tentando adivinhar o conteúdo do decreto dele? Imagino que sejam instruções para punir delinquentes. Talvez traga o diâmetro exato que os bastões afiados devem ter para cutucar os prisioneiros.

Bem, talvez nós nunca saibamos. Tenho a sensação de que os ventos cruéis dos picos devem ter sido demais para o que imagino ser um mensageiro raquítico. Talvez os companheiros da Bacia das Águas do Véu não aguentem. Eles estão muito preocupados com o Senhor Vorgoth, aquele velho lunático, para se preparar para qualquer perigo ou dificuldade a não ser o "Inimigo Ancestral"...

Deixe isso entre nós, está bem? Se os supervisores lerem isso, colocarão a minha cabeça no espeto. Um perfeitamente medido e afiado!

4110.title: Abre-te, Sésamo!
4110.text:
Abrir a porta para o Santuário Noturno foi muito fácil. O Instituto Cromwell não ensina diretamente sobre trapaças arcanas, mas a seção proibida da biblioteca nunca estava protegida... E para que ter uma seção proibida, se não para deixar os estudantes curiosos concentrarem toda a sua noite de estudos nela?

Surpreende-me não ter encontrado armamentos antigos aqui, mas o nosso adversário é ardiloso. Se meus estudos me ensinaram alguma coisa, é que as armas deles devem estar escondidas atrás de uma porta noturna diferente.

O objetivo deles é nos fazer perder o nosso tempo com charadas até cansarmos, prolongando o conflito... Mas aposto que eles não contavam com um estudante que gosta de decifrar códigos. 

É tudo ou nada. 

Darya

4111.title: Em nome da família
4111.text:
Trabalho dia e noite na construção do Posto Avançado de Bora. Mesmo assim, ainda vivemos nesta humilde cabana. Todo esse esforço, e para quê? 

Escondi alguns blocos de granito polido debaixo das escadas do posto. Na calada da noite, vou trazê-los para casa e começar a reforma para nosso filho. Nós merecemos.

4112.title: Não, Mamãe, Não me Bata
4112.text:
Você viu a nova Tirana em Obsidia? Ah, ela é assustadora.

É o jeito como ela estala o chicote nas minhas costas que me pega. Como ela se deleita ao causar dor. Aquele sorriso perverso, os dentes tortos... ahh, isso me dá arrepios.

Espero muito que ela não me bata. Ah, não, não.Espero que ela não me encontre aqui, panguando, e resolva me punir.
Ah, o que seria de mim se ela me encontrasse e me batesse como o menino sapeca que eu sou?

4113.title: Agradecemos pelo seu serviço
4113.text:
A entrega da cabeça do Ciclope será de grande benefício para nós, e sua dedicação não passou despercebida, Sargento. Já solicitamos o envio da cabeça para o laboratório mais próximo.

Notamos seu pedido por pagamentos adicionais, já que dois membros da sua tropa foram, segundo suas palavras, "destroçados pelo Ciclope, caramba!! Só sobraram as tripas!"

Vamos analisar seu pedido com o máximo cuidado. 
Não nos procure, nós entraremos em contato com o senhor.

Atenciosamente,
Escritório do Tenente Arlington, Supervisor Chefe do Programa de Expansão

4114.title: Não Invencível
4114.text:
A fera alada é formidável, é verdade.

Suas asas obscurecem nossas manhãs, enviando rajadas de vento em direção aos vales a cada descida. Seu rugido ensurdecedor reverbera pelas pedras, abalando nossas fundações e nossa fé. Ela governa os céus como se fossem seu direito de nascença. Uma campeã escolhida, nascida do coração da montanha.

Mas ela pode ser derrubada. Ela pode ser derrotada.

Eu já vi o flagelo durante o amanhecer, liberando sua chuva de fogo no horizonte como lágrimas do Sol.
Essas bolas de fogo são devastadoras no impacto... mas acredito que, com a precisão correta, podem ser aparadas e devolvidas para a bocarra da fera!

4115.title: Poderia Guardar Um Pouco de Remédio para o Ermitão?
4115.text:
Olá, Davis. Espero que esteja bem. Tenho um pedido urgente.

Conhece o ermitão da montanha atrás da ravina que às vezes vem para cá? O sujeito estranho vestido com peles que troca ametistas por suprimentos??
Ele veio de novo, mas não pediu ervas, especiarias nem vegetais. Ele pediu remédio, mas estávamos sem. Nem a bolsa cheia de ametistas que ele trouxe em suas mãos enrugadas mudariam isso.

Quando recebermos mais, poderia separar alguns para ele? Nossos soldados são prioridade, mas aquele senhor estava desesperado, então vamos reservar um pouco para quando o virmos de novo.
Aliás, se o virmos de novo. Essa jornada deve ser difícil para seus velhos ossos.

4116.title: Querida Amelie,
4116.text:
Mais um dia se foi. A neve tranquiliza o mundo lá fora, e meu coração se sente mais pesado a cada batimento. Cada nova noite compete com a anterior para ser a mais fria. Queria que você estivesse aqui para me aquecer.

Amelie, sua cadeira quebrou hoje. Tentei consertá-la, mas minhas costas protestaram. Ainda assim, não consegui jogá-la fora. Ela simplesmente fica lá, como um vestígio do passado sem utilidade além de trazer a dor da lembrança. Que dia horrível.
Se você estivesse aqui, me animaria. Encontraria você no jardim, perto das flores roxas que você adorava, com seu cabelo balançando na brisa como pétalas. Você viraria, e a luz dos seus olhos encheriam meu coração apático de brilho.

Anseio por lembrar de você apenas como aquele turbilhão lilás. Por ver você quando olho para as flores do inverno, e não para os restos quebrados de uma cadeira.
Mas é difícil, pois você está em toda parte. No que é bom e no que é ruim.
Mesmo assim, se eu pudesse fugir com você de novo, fugiria. Eu sempre escolheria você, minha pequena ametista.

4117.title: Amelie Reyk
4117.text: Você está no ar que respiro, nas lágrimas que derramo e em todos os meus devaneios.

4118.title: Rápido como um Relâmpago
4118.text:
Nossa, essa foi difícil. Com a velocidade de um relâmpago, atravessamos as catacumbas. Para honrá-lo, fiz um túmulo onde ele deu seu último suspiro...
Agora... um Feitiço de Relâmpago?! Pensei que eu estivesse perto. Estou ficando cansado disso. Acho que só sobrou uma tumba, perto de Baía d’Água Parada, em direção às colinas...

4119.title: Caminho para a Vida Após a Morte
4119.text:
Dra'Nak morreu com honra. 
Então suas garras, escamas e sangue vão para o totem. 
É o estilo de vida dos Drak. Sempre foi. 
Mantemos os fortes por perto, mesmo quando não respiram mais. Ele fica conosco, de guarda. 
Drak orgulhoso de virar totem. Chefe Drak'Dal será Totem de Madeira, Hydrak'Dal de Pedra.
Significa que se juntarão a Dalszul na vida após a morte. 
Mas se morrer em desgraça... sem ouro, sem nome... sem vida após a morte... Só esquecimento.

4120.title: Afazeres:
4120.text:
- Cuidar dos campos 
- Limpar (tirar teias de aranha!)
- Comprar velas novas -> pegar moedas do baú de prata?
                                 -> Precisa consertar a escada do porão
- Colocar barris de vinho no lugar

4121.title: Mensageiros Ancestrais de Ark Morgo
4121.text:
Ancestrais. Sim. Descendentes de Ark Morgo, eles são. Enviados como mensageiros dos deuses. Vesztah! Merphisz! Fyraszh! Arisztar! Dalszul! Para escolher novos deuses, sim. Os mais fortes entre nós!

Mas que tolos! Tolos!
Escolhem humanos! Cabeças fracas, quebram fácil! Barrigas moles e caídas! Pequenos fazedores de fogo. Bah! Fogo é fraqueza. 
Nós pisoteamos a brasa, engolimos a chama, trazemos a tempestade de sangue violeta! 

Mas humanos nos enganaram. Venceram nós em batalha, com máquinas e maldade! Injusto! 

Nós ficamos tempo demais na sombra, com vergonha. A chama dos humanos está fraca agora! Não vai queimar perto de Ark Morgo! Os corpos deles estão apodrecendo. Ossos moles, carne estragada. A hora chegou. Drak se levantam. Drak'Dal enfrenta o risco na bacia pequena. O trono espera. Ark Morgo nosso de novo!

4122.title: Reconstrução
4122.text:
Os Drak'Dal se afastaram por tempo demais. 

Todos os nossos templos viraram pó! 
Os Drak'Dal vão mostrar aos Ancestrais a verdadeira força! Que os Ancestrais cometeram um erro com humanos carnudos! Os Drak'Dal não vão construir na sombra de ninguém! 

Construam um novo lar! Construam para Dalszul! Construam, ou a Mãe da Ninhada Vesztah arrancará suas cabeças!

Rá Rá!

4123.title: Não Posso Ficar
4123.text:
Esta capela não é mais pacífica. Passaram-se os dias em que silêncio e contemplação preenchiam os salões. Agora há um discreto chacoalhar à noite que não consigo ignorar. Algo está acontecendo na cripta... e não quero estar por perto para ver como vai terminar. 

Farei minhas malas e partirei. Rezo para que nada me siga pelo penhasco, apesar de não mais acreditar que minhas preces serão ouvidas. Talvez eu siga o caminho secreto e leve minha clava só por garantia.

4124.title: Nosso Chamado Foi Atendido!
4124.text:
Cordeiros tímidos, não cabe a vocês questionar o Senhor Vorgoth e sua missão sagrada. Os deuses do vento ouviram suas preocupações e responderam com violência feroz.

Quem semear a dúvida será julgado pelos céus
Quem demonstrar medo será levado pelos Ventos do Norte
Quem largar as armas será atingido por um raio divino, como aconteceu com Rafael

Louvada seja a neve! Bendito seja o Senhor Vorgoth, Guarda do Norte e Governante de Rimgard!

3557.title: Today, I Met The Elixir Well Architect
3557.text:
Perhaps "Architect" is too grand a term — the blueprints were provided by the traveler, after all. The engineers and builders only have to fall in line. 

The monolithic structure is twofold, stretching both towards the setting sun and the sleeping core. A hollow crown reigns above to imprison within it the light of the fading moon. Its shadow is as black as its stone.

From below rises the fabled mist. Most don't see it, or pretend not to. When I brought attention to it, the workers fell silent. The "Architect" stuttered under his breath, gaze averted... his lowered head betrayed his words. He mistakes me for a madman.

My wanderer came forth from my right side and spoke to break the silence. 
"A bit of mist is to be expected. No harm will come from it. In fact, we may welcome its arrival."  The words echo in my head. We may welcome its arrival.

Yes, perhaps it will guide us. Guide our hands. Our shaking hands 
Ever shaking, leaving traces. Traces of a ghostly silhouette, reverberating
A wraith chained to its own afterimage, chasing it, spinning a vignette of fading blue
With eyelids pulled towards the moon 
Telling truth from lies, a floating spiral of the past
and present, and future, and eternity
We may welcome its arrival

— Lord Vorgoth, Guard of the North, Ruler of Rimgard

3558.title: The Lies Of A Wizened Man
3558.text:
Back in my school days, I was taught that Captain Melville liked to tell stories. Tall ones. The kind of tales that smell more like old boots than truth. As a working man, I’ve always known his tavern, "Ol’ Salt ’N Pepper", was named not just for his sea-worn beard, but because you’re supposed to take everything he says with a pinch, nay, a load of salt.

And yet, people lap it up.

They crowd around him like he’s some sea-born prophet, hanging on every crooked word. Why? The man’s a liar. A fossil. He hasn’t been out past the bay in years. Why trust a word he says — even worse, why buy his fish? Especially when we sell better catch, cheaper, and without the song and dance!

Just last week, he burst into the square, hair all tangled, shouting, "The Drak! I saw 'em, they're back!" Theatrics. Always theatrics with him.

It’s just another one of his tales, spun for coin and glory. And yet, folks eat it up.
Fools, the lot of 'em.

3559.title: The Frog Prince
3559.text:
Once upon a time, there lived a little princess with rosy cheeks and ashen hair, who loved nothing more than playing by the castle pond with her golden ball.

One day, the ball slipped from her hands and sank beneath the water. Distraught, the princess wept until a voice croaked from the reeds:
"Do not cry, little princess. I shall fetch your golden ball — for a kiss from your cherry lips!"

The girl looked up to see a lumpy frog upon a lily pad. Though repulsed, she nodded, yearning for her treasure back. The creature dove in and returned with the ball — but once the princess reclaimed her toy, she fled into the castle without so much as a thank-you.

That night, the frog came knocking on the gates. The king, upon hearing his daughter's promise, insisted she honor her word. But the princess proved reluctant evermore, and overcome by desperation, she threw the pest against a wall. 
As the pale green frog splattered against the bricks, the curse that bound him was broken, and he was freed from the shackles of his cold-blooded form. Born anew, he revealed himself to be a prince.

And so, as is custom, the underage princess was wed to a grown stranger who had tricked her into a kiss — but he was quite handsome, so all was well.

3560.title: Special Operation – Diver's Log – Entry 033 – Shit!
3560.text:
Location: You know where!!
Estimated Dive Time: Too damn long

Post Dive Findings

Time: It's dark out. No light. 
Place: No sign of Edd.

Last seen: He hit the first checkpoint, the metal grates by the overgrown terrace, behind time. Seemed winded, but steady. I thought about pulling him out. I should've stopped the mission then. Pried open the bars. Lifted him up and out of those treacherous waters.

I didn't.

The sun has set, which means Edd will have trouble finding his scheduled resurfacing spots.
Estimated dive time has been exceeded.

I think he has air for... maybe thirty more minutes, if he doesn't panic. It won't last for the way back.

We're running from grate to grate, lighting torches, yelling his name, trying to signal a safe spot to surface. But below, everything is pitch black. The deep swallows both sound and light.

I wonder if he can even still tell up from down. I wonder if he's scared. Alone. Cold. I wonder if he knows he'll die... I wonder if he'll still try to make it to the end.

3561.title: Birth Of New Gods - Dalszul
3561.text:
The young Dalszul watched as feathers rained from the skies, leaving whispy shadows underneath them as they danced. 
He pondered: "What good is conquering the skies? The land is vast and rich with treasure! We ought to thrust towards the mainland and annihilate its core! Let its blood strengthen our soil and our bodies!

And so he sank his claws into the largest mass of land he could find, and formed blocks from clay and stone to build temples to his own glory. 
Countless Drak worked and died at his walls, and when his grandest monument was finished with its final brick, he laughed: "Broodmother, hear me now! Every stretch of land, from field to forest, squeals beneath my foot! My spear can point wherever the eye can see, and still spot no edge to my domain!

As he continued his tirade, unstoppable like a boulder rolling downhill, the Drak'Dal of his clan slowly backed away. They felt a rumble in the ground, and before they knew it, a large fracture before them ripped the Earth in two.
The monument beneath their leader's feet crumbled, and Dalszul was buried beneath the rubble and dust, his blood forever marking the heart of his territory. 
Ark Morgo had taken him.

3562.title: WHAT WE GOT
3562.text:
- "Drak Slurp"
The classic. Puréed Algae in coconut water or milk.

- "Glorb Sizzle"
Bubbling mudwater enriched with ginger and a wormy surprise!

- "Sweet Sting"
Banana milk and honey. Topped with a crispy bee snack.

- Coconut Water (plain)
... with a little umbrella!

- Water
Carbonated, you animals!

For SNACKS, we got:
- More worms (alive)
- More crispy baked bees (dead)
- Half-incubated eggs (you be the judge of it)

3563.title: Special Operation – Diver's Log – Entry 032
3563.text:
Location: Submerged Temple Ruins – Coordinates Confirmed
Estimated Dive Time: 008 Hours, surfacing possible

Pre-Dive Briefing

Time: Before dusk. Docking went smoothly despite dense growths and scattered debris below.
Place: Abandoned, half-swallowed by the lake. Ideal for exploration!

Observing the parameters of the ruin confirms earlier reports. Multiple moss-ridden stairwells lay upwards, toward the gaping mouth of the temple. Structural integrity is questionable. Best we make good time and beat our own record!

I'm sure we'll find the first chamber as described by the previous team: waterlogged, more seaweed than stone, sealing the flooded pathways beyond. A mechanism or puzzle kept them from breaching the tunnels. That’s where we come in!

The team’s solid. Spirits are high. I’ve got confidence in Edd Exley — he’s sharp, steady, and knows how to handle tight spaces. 

Timing’s crucial. We’ll begin the descent at first light. With luck, the sun will be high enough to pierce through the grates and mark the resurfacing zones. 

We won't skip breakfast prep, though. Caught a few fish en route; they’ll be fine once roasted!

3564.title: Birth Of New Gods - Arisztar
3564.text:
The light of the bright, amber fountain coated the night sky as Arisztar hatched. He looked up above, and saw Fyraszh turn from flesh to fire.

"Why be confined to rocks and fiery rage?" Arisztar hushed. "To let yourself be swallowed by flames while so close to the clouds — That coward ought to jump! To fly where others fall is the greatest feat of all!"

So he took off and set his sights on the faraway cliffs. He lived high above the rest for years, hunting the birds, the vultures, and dragons above, until the Broodmother's spirit had blessed him with wings of his own. 
He became a leader unbound by the winds and soon commanded the clan of the Drak'Ari - but he would not be satisfied until he had truly soared higher than the rest. 

As he took a final leap of faith, he cried out: "Our land stretches as far as the winds blow! My wings will eclipse all below in their shadow!"
With these words, he flew closer to the sun. Silken feathers rained down as he entered Ark Morgo's halls.

3565.title: I'm Not Cut Out For This
3565.text:
My father was a soldier, but I am far from that. Who am I kidding, being stationed here alongside those broad-shouldered, valiant, violent men? Their eyes show no light. The obsidian pits simply swallow me whole, reflecting my own weakness back at me, mixed with disdain.
They don't possess kindness... their only known emotion is radiating anger, an inner heat that eats them up and warms their husks while blazing through snow and ice. 

When my father passed, the heart of this outpost was ripped away. And so was mine.
They know me. They know I'll run and hide at the first sign of trouble. It's in the way they scoff at me, in the way they snarl my name. That's why they force lookout duty upon me... even that frightens me.

Perhaps it's not so bad. Father always said "Cowards live longer."

3566.title: Wind Riders
3566.text:
Flying rings around their peaks — Far, far away
Subtle shapes and shadows, framed by the morning sun

Flaring wings to powdered beaks — Hide, hide away 
Retreat from warmth and light, when midday's rays shall come

Whirl up with a flashing gust  — At dusk, again they rise
Emerge anew from darker clouds, fly higher with the flurry

Tiny specks of silver dust — Near, near our very eyes
They've come so close, oh Flame protect us from their descending fury

3567.title: A Mind, Freed Of Chains
3567.text:
How can the night sky stay calm when it faces a sea of liars?

I feel like I'm seeing the stars for the first time. As if a dark, velvet blanket has been lifted from my eyes, allowing me to bear witness.

There was never an ancient weapon here.
We were always intruders.
What else do they not want me to know?

All these years, wasted by blindness
Sneaking past the rules of the physical world, not realizing my mind was captured just the same
I considered myself cunning while betting blindly on the cards I was handed... but it's a fool's game to share the table with liars and cheats.

I have to disappear
I have to stop this madness, this indoctrination
And I can't leave any clues or witnesses
They always spell trouble
I know that much at least

Darya

3568.title: Day 27 Midyear,  504 D.A.
3568.text:
Been a lighthouse keeper for ages. Born and raised on these shores, and proud of it, too.

The sea knows me better than my own mother. Over the years, the ripples in the water imprinted on my face, carved longing lines into my skin as I aged. My visage and story are naught but a map of the great, wide blue.
But today, I thought I spotted something... new.

It was a bright evening, clear as can be. The waters were calm under the setting sun, but I knew not to trust them. Dark clouds gathered on the horizon, foretelling a storm... and underneath them, for just a moment in the far distance, I saw something rise from below. 
A single shade against the shifting background, reaching up like a periscope, watching the shore. Watching us.
Then, it dove out of sight, disappearing from the view of my binoculars. 

It could have been driftwood. Yes, it must've been...

3569.title: Day 15 Yearwake, 506 D.A.
3569.text:
This month, we've lost more ships at sea than we ever did throughout my entire life.

I blame myself, though I know I've always upheld my duty. Every night, I light our fire to signal the safety of our harbor... I stay up, watching the pyre, stoking the flames, choking the smoke to leave only a bright merigold light... but it is not enough, and I'm losing sleep. 

Nightmares rip me from bed, force me to find my binoculars and nightgown, and make me stumble to the platform above amid darkness and rain. I thought, if I stared out long enough, I would see it. See what's causing this. Understand it. Beat it.

The storm clouds are drawing closer, and they're hiding something from me.

3570.title: Day 39 of Yearfall, 506 D.A.
3570.text:
The storm finally reached us, waves frothing with hatred and lashing at our shores.

Standing on the lighthouse platform, I felt the gusts rip at my beard and coat. I must still have salt embedded in my skin from that night's winds.

The light inside my covered oil lamp flickered, locked in a fearful dance, twisting and shifting in an effort not to be snuffed out... a repetitive plea with no one to listen, an act soaked in vain, not unlike my own.

Light the fire. Stoke the flames. Wipe down the binoculars. Look out. Light the fire again. It was pointless. The storm smothered all light.
I helplessly held on to the railing, gazing out at the night. That's when I saw it.
Rolling hills, not made of water, but made of countless bodies, rising and falling with the storm's rhythm. A wave to end us. A wave to crush us. A wave to dye the ocean red. A wave of Drak.

I dropped my binoculars and picked up my boots. If this were our death sentence, I would not die a lighthousekeeper.

3571.title: Out To Sea
3571.text:
With the Drak'Dal present, I don't think it is right to place any Cinder Vessels down. Its inhabitants may not be saved but imprisoned by a metal cocoon. They could be pried open too easily, falling prey to these beasts... and their Ancient encasing won't save them then.

Therefore, we're setting our sights on the horizon, as planned. I hope to find a ship in Stillwater Bay to charter... perhaps then, we'll see how far the rot has spread and will trace its path on a map.

I wonder if it's right... not to turn around, not to ride towards the flying islands where the Elder Ancients linger... not to defend them despite their rigidity, not to bring my brother to his knees before he barges through their gates. But with what army? With what might?

We ought to live. For the future, and for everyone who depends on us. On me. For you, Emily.
When I come back, I will weave daylilies into your hair and serenade you with my lyre until my voice grows hoarse. One day. I promise.

— Queen Jezmina of Orindell

3572.title: Last Words
3572.text:
I see now that this is the end.
I saw my sisters die. I saw them get torn apart, swallowed by one of those horrendous beasts. I can still hear their screams. I think they will haunt me in death.

They warned me of the risks. I went anyway, pushing the doubts aside.
Even now, surrounded by blood, I cannot say that standing with them was wrong. I would rather die knowing that I did not abandon my sisters than live knowing that I had.

Our cause was just, and our intentions were pure. Be certain, I would choose this path again. 
At last, we are reunited with our true queen. 
Glory to Queen Pikemead. 

- Celia, Guard of the Blood Rose

3573.title: The Oath We Swore
3573.text:
We swore to protect our Queen and her lands, and to never let royal blood get spilled. Even now, over 20 years after her demise, that oath still binds us.

It's no surprise that not many of us are willing to spill Vorgoth's blood, it will cost us our titles. They call us dissenters because we refuse to look away. They say to raise the blade against royal blood is the death of honor, but what honor is there in apathy.

The island has cast us into exile. It's monastery will never open it's doors for us ever again, but we will not be silenced. We will not bow. We will protect what we believe in until the very end.

For the Queen we swore to. For the realm she loved.

3574.title: ONLY TODAY: The Fabulous Godwin's "Impalement Act!"
3574.text:
We're celebrating Lord Vorgoth's successful securing of the summits! All glory to the Guard of the North!

Get your tickets now before they sell out! Check out the show in the upper grand hall on the 20th of Midyear, 496 D.A.— refreshments are not included!!

3575.title: All Preparations Are Done!
3575.text:
I sharpened the knives, patched the hole in my pants, and most importantly, re-attached the little jingly-bells to my hat! The stage looks alright, too. I don't think that the throwing distance will be a big issue. Everything's ready for the performance.

I wish I'd had more time to practice, but what's the worst that could happen? I've done this number countless times, so I'm sure it'll be alright.

3576.title: I Want To Ride The Winds!
3576.text:
I sympathize with Marsha's apprehension. Really, I do. It's in her nature to be cautious; she's a "Hophare" at heart — always a mere breath away from skittering off, dashing to safety and comfort.

Well, regarding animals, I'm more of a Whitewing Vulture... I'm bound to the skies! It's my calling to glide above these freezing valleys! 

How can Marsha not feel intrigued by the upstreams outside our cabin? By the landing site just beyond the winds? 
Just how high up would they take me, I wonder? Perhaps far enough to reach the giant skeleton by the ridge? ...How steep would the fall be, dared I make a mistake?

Alas, there's no point in pondering it. I don't want to break my little snow rabbit's heart. Or my bones.

3577.title: Descending The Halls
3577.text:
The Halls have beckoned me for a long time. I've ignored their call in ages past, but now, I stand emboldened by the men behind me. Valiant, undaunted soldiers armed to the teeth. They said they'd follow me anywhere, into any dark, any depth. 

This cursed sanctuary shan't taint our peaks any longer. Do not fret, Brother. If we fall, we fall together.

I plan to return at first light — Should the sun rise without me, send aid.

Berhtolf, Firstborn of the Dimwealds

3578.title: Firstborn Folly
3578.text:
My brother's always been the insolent sort. Right of the firstborn, he'd claim as he dove headfirst into battle. This Hollow Hall taunts him, and emboldened by his entourage, I fear he's to rebuke its mockery.

Alas, he's chosen to drag himself and his troops into the shadowed caverns... while I'm left to await his return with bated breath.
I've gathered my men; rowdy sorts with a dire need for coins in their pockets. Their loyalty is paid for, but there's no telling how the dungeons may test this bond.

There's no time to waste. Berhtolf may already be held at a sword's edge, or buried beneath ice and rubble.

Every minute counts.
Lando Dimweald

3579.title: We Won't Share Our Breath With You
3579.text:
Climb upon the highest mountain and peer over the snow-blessed rim. Gaze into the swirling white, into the spiraling void. Just across the horizon, illuminated by the rising sun's light, is our land — and our gate to the stars, now barred.

Hear this: We aim to ascend, to rise, to flee — to leave the rotting lands below, corrupted by the spreading roots and blossoms of a familiar seed.
We yearn to return to the celestial light and purity of our cosmic blood.

Anything — or anyone — untamed, impure, or foolish must remain, even our youngest flames. Our doors are locked to you.
Do not pry them open.

3580.title: Two Tribes, Two Flames
3580.text:
I finally understand why the obelisk glyphs gave me so much trouble. 
Their language changed. It split into different dialects, one young, one old. Two factions within the Ancient breed, and two ideals: 

The young Ancients chose to come to our aid — they chose to help us fight the Shroud. To share their fire so humanity could withstand what they accidentally awoke. 
Despite this, the elder Ancients still clung to stoic elevation, segregation, and neutrality... thus, sealing themselves away and ascending to preserve the Flame's purity.

I've gone so far... Survived the Shroud, the heat, the cold... now, what else is there to do but validate my hypothesis? If I can read their signs, walk their path... I can speak their language... ask questions... and get answers.

— Loraine Crim, Yearfall, 508 D.A.

3581.title: I Want To Go Home
3581.text:
I was carrying ammunition to the ballista with Connor when Howling Peak suddenly roared. Squinting towards the rising smoke, I saw something hiding inside, causing the vapor to swirl... When it broke from the veil of gray, I froze. Screams erupted.

Amidst the chaos, a familiar voice called out. "George, get it together! I'll light the balefire, and you shoot!" Connor grabbed a torch and sped towards the bridge. The sky was darkened by wings. His silhouette was tinged in shadow as he vanished into black.

With shaking hands, I fired a bolt. Then two. Three — all missed. Unbothered, the winged beast spewed a hot, foul cloud from its mouth that melted our walls. It caught Connor on his way up. That's the last thing I saw before I fainted.

I want to go home, but they won't let me. We ain't in the barracks anymore. This is the real deal.

— George

3582.title: My First Day With The Expansion Program
3582.text:
We're not in the barracks anymore. This is the real deal. The new frontline, fresh and freezing! Time to put on a tough face, or else my new mate Connor will pick on me.

Everyone around me is a proper soldier, braving the cold for the motherland. How exciting!! 
Right now, I'm only chopping wood and shooing away rats, but that's gonna change, believe me! I overheard the others talk about some gigantic winged beast while sitting near the ballistae... 

They won't tell me what it is, but I'll soon see for myself. And when I do, I'll pierce its eye with a single shot! That's sure to impress Connor!
— George

3583.title: Gliding Contest!
3583.text:
We're proud to announce that we will host the annual gliding contest on Day 40 of Midyear, 502 D.A. again! 

As last time, the goal is to jump off the large wooden platform outside the sleeping quarters and glide in a slight curve towards the landing platform on the right-hand side.
Don't miss those upstreams, or you won't reach the platform! The best glider gets a reward at the end!
If you're up for the challenge, write your name below! 

Kip Dipper 
Ryan the Ragged 
"Lucky" Chester Loft
Abraham Walz

3584.title: The Last Attack Was Devastating
3584.text:
Our numbers are decimated, and morale is low.

The warriors amongst us may hide behind their swords and shields, and the mages could call upon the power of the elements... but us archers, what can we do? The beast makes our arrows look like mere toothpicks!

There may be ways to whittle it down, however. I've been working on more stun arrows... they've the potential to force that wretched animal to the ground momentarily, allowing the others to strike! Maybe there's a way to make similar ammunition for our ballistas...? 

Until I figure that out, these stun arrows will have to do. When the creature comes back, we'll be ready!

3585.title: Moving Shapes
3585.text:
I always thought this lookout job was the most boring thing in the world. Boy, was I wrong. 

I keep seeing something in the distance — shuffling between gusts of wind, clouded by fog and mist. It's near the valley's tomb, so I thought it was another Hollow. An aimless puppet, skeletal and frail... but that's not right. 

It looks towards me every night. I can't see it, but I feel it. It's half alive, half dead... some visitor from beyond for Hollow's Eve, maybe. 

My resignation letter has already been sent. I can't wait to get back to boring work.

3586.title: Harbor Log, Day 13 of Yearwake, 503 D.A.— Abandon Ship!!
3586.text:
I gave in to my suspicion tonight and slipped aboard the vessel. The soldiers had turned their backs, staring off into the distance, fixated on a point beyond the horizon... unmoving. It was the perfect time to strike.

A dockmaster ought to know what passes through his harbor, no matter whose seal it bears, I say! So I snuck into the cargo hold, careful not to let the iron grate cover slip from my trembling hands. The air below smelled rotten. Infested. Could it be rats, or some dead stowaway? I covered my nose and mouth with a handkerchief and pressed on, making my way to the back of the hold where the crates were stacked.

Once there, I broke one's seal and recoiled at the sight that revealed itself before me.
The cases were not filled with grain or powder, but with some choking fog — sealed inside like a thing alive, pressing against its confines, rebelling. No markings, no warning. Just a pale mist festering on a bed of foul mushroom flesh.

Does the Lord seek to spread a sickness to distant shores? My vessels should ship food and clothing, not a new form of warfare crueler than steel! 
I am resigning tomorrow... may the next sod bear witness to what comes next.

3587.title: Latte Recipe
3587.text:
Brew the ground beans in water as is custom,
then soften the brew with milk until the bitterness fades.

The result: a smooth, warm, and pleasant cup
I'd like to call this creation: Latte

3588.title: Black Coffee Recipe
3588.text:
One for tough warriors:

Take roasted beans, ground fine as dust,
and mingle them with hot water.
Let the brew be dark and bitter — a strong potion
to rouse the spirit and quicken the mind.

3589.title: It Taints The Water Red
3589.text:
Something has awoken, I fear.

More people go missing each eve... first, t'was only those who ventured past the bay. But now, anyone too close to the canals during a moonless night is lost to the waters.

I feel like something is testing us... biting down to see if we flinch, fight, or flee. But what can we do in the face of a nameless specter that's come with a challenge? There are no guards, no lord left to defend us... They've set off to fight a holy war and left us behind, near dark waters hiding sinister fates. 

Some people chose to move further inland. Even the lighthousekeeper has fled, or so I heard. An old man who spent his entire life by this coast... I wonder what he saw last night, during that sunless storm... and how long we have until it reveals itself.

3590.title: Wine And Seafoam
3590.text:
Once, as a seamstress, I had quite the popular customer — the old Captain himself!

I will never forget the dawn at which he stumbled through my open doors, beard not nearly as ashen as it is today, little more than a stained shirt on his body.
"Morn', young lass!" He cawed with a hoarse voice, "I'd like a new coat! Deep blue as the sea, with gold and glamor, I'd say — hick!"

While taking his measurements, I observed him closely. He smelled of wine and was missing not only his coat, but one shoe... When I asked him about it, he said:
"Nay, the wine is half the story — See, as I was out late on the canal, an old devil born from the frothing blue called to me from below! He said he'd trade me a bottle of his finest for one button of my coat! A bottle for a button? I thought: Why not? But as I reached down to receive the wine, the impish creature pulled me in by my cufflinks and turned back seafoam! Hick! I went overboard, mayday, mayday! They had to fish me and my boat out — and my coat, it was gone with the waves! Hick!"

I had his new jacket ready within three days, but I always wondered how his old clothes didn't wash ashore. Did they turn into seafoam, too?

3591.title: Sweet Mocha
3591.text:
A sweet comfort in weary hours:

Grind the beans and steep them in water —
add sugar, that the flavor be full and kind

A Sweet Mokka is prepared.

3592.title: The Worst Has Occurred!
3592.text:
...We're out of coffee, so if you're looking to come in and relax, the best we can offer is tea.

We may have a spare machine in the attic, but the top levels of the tower need repairs, so it's not safe to ascend. Of course, if anyone out there is willing to risk their life for it, we'll promise free coffee for the foreseeable future.

Best of luck!

3593.title: Harbor Log, Day 12 of Yearwake, 503 D.A.— Personal Notes
3593.text:
The crown sent word.
We ought to prepare a new vessel for its maiden voyage, but the ship’s to be sent off with cargo none of us are allowed to inspect. Strange business. Crates bear no marks, no writs, no tally for the ledger... and they're sealed shut.

The Lord deems them of such weight that his own men were dispatched to see them stowed. Thought I’d see sharp-eyed veterans, but the lot that stumbled in yesterday looked half-dead, eyes glazed and dragging their boots. They’re fixing cannons to a merchant hull... my hull. Never seen the like. 

I know not the purpose of this lading, only that it sits ill with me. Shouldn't I know what shipments come and go like the back of my hand?

3594.title: Ones We Carved Ourselves
3594.text:
Two bloods laid siege to these lands.

One was cold and violet as a yearfall's plum, encased in emerald leaves like scales. The other red and warm as a song shared by the fireside.

A forsaken clash, brought forth by our favoritism of fire. When we lifted humanity, we lowered all else... trampled a seed that thought us to be its sun, its god. But the seed grew in silence and hate, and where one purple petal fell, its roots took hold.

3595.title: Mushy Humans
3595.text:
Large ship stranded on our shores.

Spoiled food, rotten wood. Merphisz would laugh at the state of it.

Clouds swirling around, misty blue like fog on the horizon, but murky. Humans inside, or something once human. Mushy and soft, rip open to reveal glowing hearts still beating in an unfamiliar rhythm. 

Weaklings! Ancients chose the wrong champions! Now is the time of the Drak! Drak'Dal will cross the open waters and squish the puny fleshlings! Rebuild the empire! 

For Dalszul!

3596.title: My Ancestors And I Grew Up In These Tunnels
3596.text:
Our family worked tirelessly to chisel ever-winding shafts into the stone, though all of them are gray and dull. It's hard for me to imagine a different life, lest I gaze at the water nearby and remember my youth.

I remember reading about a mermaid: A lonely maiden whose heart melted into the waves as she turned to seafoam. Years in the mine made me forget, made me grow up. But not all let go of such fairytales.

Once, I met a man with legs that should've been fins. The Siren Seeker, they called him — always caressing the sea as if it were his lover, letting the tide envelop him as he dove for treasures below.
He was collecting sun-bleached seashells by the shore as I asked:
"What do you seek in the water that you can't find on land? Shouldn't you take up proper work and settle down?"

Without looking up, he mumbled through a smile: "I seek the kiss of a mermaid — one who hides her voice in conch shells and words in bottled messages. I'll save her from turning to foam, and me from falling to gray. " 

Today, I recall the Seeker's words, retrace the pages of that fairytale book in my mind. I understand now. Our family worked tirelessly to chisel ever-winding shafts into the stone, all of which are gray and dull. I wish I hadn't forgotten the magic from yonder years. I wish I had carved my own path and set sail.

3597.title: Hot Spring Time!
3597.text:
Being a "Scavenger" is so limiting, dull, and... grimy.

Perhaps you shouldn't have to spend all day drinking and fighting. What if a man wants to take a bath instead? A pure, beautiful, calm, scented soak in the Cromville Hot Spring?

I don't want to cut and tear, I yearn to splish and splash — to enjoy a steamy bubble bath with my lads, at a comfortable yet sensible distance! We could even dive for treasure! That's "manly", no? It would be fun!

People propose that my rugged physique ought to dictate my tastes, but why be covered in grease when you could smell like rose water? I refuse to yield to such a pretense!

3598.title: Gotta Fix That Fence
3598.text:
I can't have my goats wander off with these one-eyed beasts nearby.

I don't know where their goddamn cave is, but I sure hope they stay there. Can't stand to lose another goat... meat supply is runnin' awfully low, and I won't go back to eating rats!

3599.title: Who Is Scared Of Flying Horrors?
3599.text:
Who is scared of flying horrors? 
Winged beasts, up in the sky!

Who is scared of flying horrors? 
Behind clouds, they're hiding high!

Who is scared of flying horrors?
Is it you, or is it me?

Those who fear will sleep in sorrow
And the brave will sleep in peace!

3600.title: Worried About Junior
3600.text:
I'm worried about Junior. 

I've worked so hard to create a good life for him — one that shields him from war and death... yet, whether it's childish defiance or a wish to follow his father's footsteps, Junior refuses to feel comforted by our quaint existence. 
He won't let go of this dream of becoming a soldier... a nightmare in disguise, I'm afraid. If he could just settle down and take over the salon instead, I'm certain he'd live a better, or at least, longer life!

3601.title: Never Whole
3601.text:
The person I buried wasn't my father anymore. He was a changed man, captivated and twisted by a sword from the stars that should've never landed in his grasp.

He found it when I was still a child. Afterwards, I saw him hunched over shuffled papers every night. His long, thinning hair covered his face in oily strands, hanging into his lap, where he cradled the blade. In my eyes, his crooked neck made him look like a weeping willow.
He wouldn't even turn to meet my gaze. "Tell me, where's your twin, little one?" He murmured to the saber. "Come hither, make me whole again."

Now, many years, later, I am hunched over my own desk like father once was. His last wish was to be buried with his sword. I obliged. Did I do the right thing? He didn't die by the blade, but that sword took his life...

3602.title: Understanding The Ancient Enemy
3602.text:
Ain't no way we can break through these defenses.

Looks like the Ancients set up these beacons to protect their border.
Every time we set foot behind the line, someone gets zapped, fried, or pulverized. Lord Vorgoth won't like this at all...

If we want to cross the threshold to their territory, we'll have to tear down some beacons... or find a way to deactivate them. If we're victorious... no, when we're victorious, then the ancient gates will be right at our fingertips.

Office of Lieutenant Arlington, First Overseer of the Expansion Program

3603.title: What A Lucky Bastard!
3603.text:
We all jumped off the starting platform in Iron Heart. Me, Ryan, that new Chester guy, and Abraham. 
Ryan didn't get far; he plummeted to the ground like a wet grain sack. Go figure. Abraham and I made it here just fine, eyes on the prize. But when I turned around to check on Chester, I became glued to something else.

Chester's glider must have ripped. He was tossing and turning in the air, tumbling between the gusts of wind, rising and falling aimlessly.
He's one lucky bastard, however. Got grabbed by an ice vulture mid-flight, probably mistaking him for some prey! It took him away to the far end of the mountain reaches.
 
That's a 50% survival chance for the annual gliding contest. Better than last year, at least.
— Kip Dipper

3604.title: Excavation Protocol, No. 2
3604.text:
The root has been more "active" as of late, reacting to the stimuli around it as if awoken. According to the enclosing rock formations and their geological records, this organism may have slumbered for thousands of years. However, we may not be its first guests. 
While it refuses to be catalogued properly, it always holds to a similar core; a codex of matter that appears entirely external — not mycelial or plant-like. Not human. Not Ancient, either. Whatever it is, it was absorbed in bygone ages, therefore predating our records.

Its past is riveting, but so is its future. We've distilled the roots into a liquid — a shimmering blue Elixir, captivating and serene — and stored it for further testing.

Surprisingly, it was gone when I walked by storage today. No signs of unpermitted intrusion... Only a scrap of dark, tattered fabric in the rubble. I was worried until a belated order for inventory transfer arrived. My assistants must have re-organized samples ahead of schedule.

The dead skincells on the fabric present with the same matter codex as the fungal roots, so the scrap was likely here all along. I wonder what existed first: The root, or the lifeform sampled by it?

- Manathor; Expedition Lead

3605.title: Test Subject No. 72 - Fungal Root
3605.text:
Summary: 
A fungal organism composed of transformative cells capable of adhering to and consuming organic matter. Assimilated material is either replicated or altered into novel biological structures.

Properties: 
Mycelial. Dormant. Feeds on organic matter. 

Research Category: 
Medicinal; Longevity.

Research Note: 
Growth appears cyclical rather than linear. The organism may exist in a perpetual sequence of expansion, bloom, decay, and renewal. Further observation is required to determine whether these phases are environmentally triggered or intrinsic to its biology.

3606.title: Excavation Protocol, No. 1
3606.text:
The excavation was successful. The following analysis — not so much.

I was there when we uncovered the cave room. Finding it was easy, for it made its presence known from the moment we broke ground. Fine tendrils crept across the stone like vines, spindly and thin at first, then thicker and sluggish further down. They outlined a path all the way to the heart.

First inspection would lead one to believe that what lingers before us is a large, decomposing fungal root... yet, what shows up under the microscope is anything but. 

The organism is alive, still. Undying, and refusing to be analysed or understood. It re-shapes itself upon being observed, latching onto nearby cells and matter, consuming, mimicking, changing them. It is utterly fascinating.

Such properties hold great potential! We ought to dig deeper, push further — perhaps these roots could hold the secret to a longer life... to eternity, even!

- Manathor; Expedition Lead

3607.title: Test Subject No. 72 - Fungal Root
3607.text:
Summary: 
A fungal organism composed of transformative cells capable of adhering to and consuming organic matter. Assimilated material is either replicated or altered into novel biological structures.

Properties: 
Mycelial. Dormant. Feeds on organic matter. 

Research Category: 
Medicinal; Longevity.

Research Note: 
Growth appears cyclical rather than linear. The organism may exist in a perpetual sequence of expansion, bloom, decay, and renewal. Further observation is required to determine whether these phases are environmentally triggered or intrinsic to its biology.

3608.title: Proto Vessel Storage Handover Report
3608.text:
Good news: I managed to stow away the vessels after all. Finished right on time for the solstice — We're prepped. Told you not to doubt me, didn't I? 
You were right about the climate, though. It's downright awful — but perfect for conservation, I suppose. I've wrapped myself in layers for every shift, and suggest you do the same. 

The cold isn't the only thing giving me shivers. Did you see the guard construct? Forgot what they call it... Creepy thing. Why so many legs...?
At least it'll keep the Proto Vessels safe during Code Violet... Engineers said something about this being "V1", meaning some doors will shut permanently once the alarm is raised. It'll be a hassle to complete repairs in the chamber like that, so watch out and don't get locked in! 
If you do, well, I hope you brought warm garb.

See you after my vacation!

3609.title: Frozen Eternity
3609.text:
Hmm… maybe if I cast this spell on myself long enough, I can shock-freeze my body — and then thaw whenever I wish. That way, I could extend my life… right? Right?!
I’ve done it! I made it!

3610.title: The Luscious Drakonian Maid, Chapter 3: Beneath Cloth
3610.text:
Sir Lancehart: 
Dearest Lush, this disguise will serve thee well. The human garb hides thine emerald scales — with this, all shall see thee as a common milkmaid! Only I will know the truth of thine pure heart and exotic curves!

Lush'Kyss: 
You wish to leave the cover of the canopy together, and live unbound from hate and prejudice... but this cloth is woven of lies! None shall accept me as I hide my deepest desires!

Sir Lancehart:
Do not discard your disguise, Lush'Kyss! We've strayed too far from the thicket! Say, how will thee suffer when a stranger's gaze finds thine flower?

Lush'Kyss: 
Then they may marvel at its divinity! These covers are chains I must break to rid myself of shame! See my claws run across my trembling chest, unabashed! Oh, how would I hide a racing heart such as this, my beloved? Each beat compels me ever forward and into thine embrace! Come, soothe my craving as you did by the silver riverside!

Sir Lancehart:
Thine garden has blossomed, dear! Oh, fire overtakes me! I must wet my lips with thine nectar to quench the thirst!

Lush'Kyss: 
Plant your seed, my beloved! You have my explicit and verbal consent!

Sir Lancehart:
...And I'd never lay a hand on thee with ambiguity overshadowing our bond, as I hold thee in too high a regard!

3611.title: Letter Of Resignation
3611.text:
Dear Supervisor,
I had hoped to write this note respectfully to thank you for the opportunity to work here, but I can’t keep up the pretense anymore. The truth is, this job is breaking me. The labor is too much: day after day of swinging tools until my body gives out, only to collapse into miserable tents that barely shield us. It’s inhuman.

And now, the fog. That damned fog creeps in from the rear shafts. None of us know what it is, but we all feel it. The headaches, the shaking hands, the strange dreams — don't tell me it's nothing because we all know it's not. Some of the men already look like shadows of themselves.

I won't be next. I won't wait until the mine and the fog consume me completely. I quit. Let someone else break their back and lose their mind for you. If the ore is so important to you, you can dig it out yourself.

3612.title: Vorgoth And The Moon
3612.text:
He's always up there in that lonely tower.

Instead of parlaying with his men, or what's left of 'em, he's staring at the stars... why? It must be the Wanderer's doing. He's the one who's been infecting his mind; guiding his hand, his sword...

What answer, what wisdom could the moon overhead possibly hold? Is the Lord growing sentimental? No, it can't be. 

It must be his way of preparing for the siege.

3613.title: Many Voices Cry As One
3613.text:
I keep hearing whispers in the dark. They're faint. Far away, but amplified... manifold. Layered. Like an echo that answers its own beck and call. A folded veil, descending on itself.

As I attempt to peel back the pleats, it feels as though I brush against skin above skin; skin where there should be none, should never have been.
A thing that grows and never stops growing, painting over itself with matter. A thing with many faces; crying from many mouths.
Heckling, deceiving, bantering.

Cinder's Cradle has finally done me in.
The others fell - or surrendered themselves - to the Shroud long ago... for me, the final stab was this sweltering heat... and all these... voices.

For the longest, I couldn't place them. I recognize them as unlike my own, unlike my comrades' or the Lord's...

Then, I realized it. When the Wanderer spoke, raising his fist firmly by Vorgoth's right side, I heard it.

I heard the voice of the whispers, split from many mouths.

3614.title: Breach
3614.text:
Our onslaught on the Ancient gate was met with little resistance. Thus, its stone was promptly crushed to dust beneath the march of my men.

The Ancients are trying to lull me... they've sapped energy from their barriers to fuel the cloistered weapon in their midsts! This is a declaration of war — so war they shall get!

I can see their fabled Citadel in the distance... proudly crossing the horizon's line; ripping through the waxing moon's light!
This is where they keep their flame, so my wandering friend says... where they will summon fire to rain down on MY people, scorching the earth of MY lands!

The reign of rats must end...Together, we must tear them down.
Down the gullet. Down the spiral. 
Down, down, down 
to us.

— Lord Vorgoth, Guard of the North, Ruler of Rimgard

3615.title: There's Something About Andrew
3615.text:
As far as I can remember, it's always been just the three of us. Andrew, Harriot, and I — and the fish, of course. Our little roost near the ice hole has been our home, and we never strayed far from it.

The sun was setting, and Harriot was storing her newest trophy — a typical evening. As we were packing up, Andrew decided to stay behind to "fish" alone... but I saw that glint in his eye, that look towards the back of the cave. An explorative urge had struck him. Maybe he hoped for clearer waters, a catch of his own? Who knows...

Ever since then, he's changed. Last I saw him, he had glossy eyes and a raspy cough. It made the fish elude him more than usual. Despite this, Harriot reeled in a big one — A slippery Crimsonback, almost too heavy for her frail arms to lift.
Andrew ripped the fish out of her hands and, without hesitation, slid it off the hook and into his gullet. When Harriot protested, he swiftly silenced her with a push, nearly knocking her off our deck and into the water.

We left early that day, without Andrew. Harriot sought to return and "make things right" between them, but I fear our friend is beyond help... something crept inside him as he wandered the bowels of this cave. I have to keep it out. For good.

3616.title: Starving
3616.text:
I'm starving
They want me to rot

Never sharing
Always pretending to care

My stomach is rumbling, and I cannot rest
Can't catch my breath... something sits inside my lungs, choking me

I need fresh fish
Fresh blood
But they won't ever share — She deserved it
And if you don't open up
Nils
I will come for you too
And I will get you like I got Harriot

3617.title: Beginning Of Time
3617.text:
Long ago, we lost a piece of our star.
It ripped through the void, a bright streak against the dark, fleeing our sight. A flash from something to nothing... the light of ghosts, the memory of home.
The spectre turned scout; for it crashed into a planet most promising. It formed the heart in Embervale's midst — Illuminating a hollow in which rainwater pooled, and life began to bloom.

A fascinating first. A kaleidoscope of potential.
We had to see it for ourselves.

Stoic and stalwart as they were, the twin mountains allowed our entry. We sampled, scored, and savored all we could before turning our gaze back to the firmament... when the guards of creation denied our leave, barring the gate inside the crimson core. We pleaded and begged.
It was not enough.

Fire, fire, burning pyre. We scorched a hole into the sky. The mess we made let the moonlight reach low; reach us — chaining the sea of stars inside a marble that hung above like a taunt. 
One could imagine their palms outstretched, clasping around something that cannot, will not be touched. It was out of reach.
It was not enough.

Our gaze turned inward. Downward. Searching for a source beyond Flame and Spark inside the core. That's where we found it. Another subject to prod.
The rotting fruit with a thousand seeds, asleep, yet breathing — then rousing, reeling, reaching.
We left it buried, sealed beneath words of warning and layers of grime.

We were not enough.

3618.title: Hours In The Bath?
3618.text:
Lately, Maynard has made a habit of bathing during his break. 

I don't mind so much — I prefer him smelling of rosewater and candlewax to his usual grime and gruff. But he takes HOURS in there, leaving me alone to herd the poor sods in the cells! 

He thinks he's such a sly fox, too — as if I don't see the book he hides under his towel whenever he sets off. I don't care what smut he reads, but can't he hurry with it?

3619.title: To Caleb: Gauntlets Are Done
3619.text:
I've put them in a chest inside the forge. Careful when you take 'em out — they're hot. 

I'll take a break now. Don't look for me. I won't work on anything else until these burns clear up.

3620.title: At The Castle Gates!
3620.text:
It's the first day of yearfall, 502 D.A. and I've finally reached the castle, and whilst preparing for my little soliloquy, I could not help but let my mind wander! 

How shall I ever memorize my lines whilst dreaming beneath such magnificent architecture? I thought the statues of our Lord that line the town entrance fed my hungry eyes, but it seems they were merely an appetizer! The stonework here holds space for scenery, I say:

These columns reach toward the dome like prayers on a rainy night, coating the citadel in an awe-inspiring serenity. Imagine a gray chapel atop a cliff, moss creeping through the century-old brick. Thunder and lightning haunt not only the sanctuary, but the rivulet choking its precipice.
Stone arcs spring from side to side, frogs leaping across the rippling stream. They span 'round the pilasters like the skeleton of an umbrella, sheltering us sheep from the howling winds.

I must not forget myself! My audience is drawing near — I hope the Lord will savor my voice! If not, I might hang from one such arc soon enough... Focus, Chester! Grim thoughts ought not to be in a blond and pretty head like yours!

— "Lucky" Chester Loft

3621.title: Surrounded By Cowardice And Secrecy
3621.text:
Out of all the realms under the ever-stretching skies, I've been burdened with the wildest. Half my dominion lies strangled in vines; every root and rock conspires against my claim.

My men are too weak-hearted to gain control of the old ruins. A trap laid in a watery tomb sends them scattering like vermin. Not one among them dares lay hammer to the temples, to grind them to dust so that order may reign once more. It may be wiser to turn eastward... the peaks aren't haunted by memory.

Meanwhile, my dear siblings have summoned me to the annual ball — a tiresome charade of civility, forcing me to leave my throne unguarded. Do they not see the peril? My borders serve as the only defense against the conniving trickster gods! Mayhaps their invitation is yet another trap, another tomb to drown in...!
...Foolish thought. The vines enrapture my mind, wrapping me in paranoia. I shall attend, as duty commands — and I will urge them to build ballistas, not "Night Sanctums". Offering wisdom to a wordless horde... Truly, my kin have grown indulgent, bewitched by the Ancients’ secrecy.

I must rest. Before dawn, I shall attend the audience of a wanderer who's wormed his way into my court. He claims to bear a gift from beyond. I will hear him. He promises diversion. 

— Lord Vorgoth, Guard of the North

3622.title: Begrudgingly, I Joined My Family's Reunion
3622.text:
Such a trivial pursuit, now that I've tasted eternity... but I did not go without a plan, nor a convincing argument.

Just one drop of the Elixir to sweeten the wine. That was all it took for Gormander, old fool, to call forth his advisers and engineers. They may caution him against building the Elixir Wells at first, but their words will wither soon enough.

Jezmina, however, could only be silenced through a swift backhand. The brat still believes the Ancients may have good reason to hide such power... A private contractor will build the Wells in her stead, should she not oblige. Once her yammering faded into weeping, I forced her eyes open and told her the truth amongst lies.

The Ancients HID this from us! 
They're sleeping snakes, and all but me are too fearful to wake them! Cowards, I say! Rats before Dragons in disguise, I tell you!

We are right to defend ourselves. Dig just a little deeper — What else lies hidden below?
