Will Earth spill her secrets if we split her tongue, crack her open, leave her bleeding?

I trust only the mist under the wanderer's hood, the twitch of his shadow, the gaping of his hundred mouths 
He can make us rise
Can make us levitate
Can change the mice to men

— Lord Vorgoth, Guard of the North, Ruler of Rimgard

3623.title: I Had The Most Enthralling Time Today
3623.text:
The wanderer arrived on the 49th Day of Midyear, 492 D.A., as promised — a gust of freezing winds trailing him. As he entered my throne room, an unsettling mist lingered where he stepped.

His face was cloaked to hide a ghastly sickness... a kind I had never laid eyes on before. His flesh was pale and tinged blue; his face lacking symmetry as if he had suffered a stroke in years past - or as if he had been assembled, not born. Such a pitiful being.

Thin hands held out a bright blue flask, shimmering in the candlelight. A weapon, he called it. A secret... hidden from us by the Ancients.
He needed not say more. I had long been aware that the tricksters only reveal what they please.

I grasped the flask and I gulped down the mystery inside. Dust motes began to swirl at the edges of my vision. Mist rose around me, enveloping each breath I took... crept inside me, breached my heart, my skull, and settled behind my eyes. It was pulling. Pulling upwards, towards my eyelids, fluttering, til my feet left the palace carpet.

Levitation. I floated above the ruins, above the vermin, the cowards, the liars.

Once I reunited with the familiar ground below, the wanderer flashed a smile. He had given me both means and reason to strike.
My hands shake, still... but I must grip my blade firmly.

— Lord Vorgoth, Guard of the North, Ruler of Rimgard

3624.title: Rudimentary Drak Writing
3624.text:
(The writing is crude, and the signs are written with short, apathetic scratches. A plaque reads: Example for rudimentary Drak writing, found by fishers dredging near the archipelago. Presumed age: Recent.)

Drak'Mer weak. Why breed underwater? Lay eggs in ponds? Waste of time.

Dalszul would never. Would build temples. Adorned in gold. Would force humans, brick by brick. 

Young Drak should hatch and stomp their feet! Should stick spears in land that belongs to them! Not splish and splash! 
That's why Drak'Dal strong! Big muscles! Lift stone! Spill blood!

Hail Dalszul! Rah Rah!

3625.title: Advanced Drak Writing
3625.text:
(The engravings are delicate, and each stroke seems carefully placed. A plaque at the bottom reads: Example of advanced Drak writing, reclaimed from a flooded temple. Presumed age: over 1000 years old)

Hail Vesztah, the great Broodmother.

She, who grew from a single droplet of blood.
She, who rose from the sea of chaos in the eye of the storm.

She, who wove the waves for Merphisz.

She, who ignited the heart of Fyraszh.

She, who bestowed wings onto Arisztar.

She, who gifted Dalszul gold and gallows.

She, who is both mother and maw
The womb and the grave
Giver and Destroyer
The great ruler of Ark Morgo

In her womb, we grow
In her lap, we begin
Under her watch, we suffer or succeed
And in her grasp, we shall end

3626.title: To The Castle!
3626.text:
Ah, it feels proper to plant my boots back on solid ground! Masquerading as a soldier was an interesting intermission, but dancing with the winds as a glider connoisseur was most thrilling, I believe!

Still, deep down, I remain a humble minstrel — a slave to the melody that bleeds from my aching heart! Yes, I declare: T'was the urge to create that brought me back — so says my newly discovered fear of vultures. They haunt not only the heights 'round my former outpost, but my dreams, as well... no matter!

I've returned to the love of my life: music! And thus, my mistress demands I try my luck at the Lord’s court! I hear the fellow’s got good taste and a sharp tongue for those who offend it. I may either join his banquet, or range of hunting trophies — but worry does not suit me. Besides, danger to a daring bastard is like a raindrop on a rose. 
It simply sweetens the eve.
- "Lucky" Chester Loft

3627.title: Drak — Linguistic Degeneration
3627.text:
The differences between these creatures are to be contextualized not as natural variance, but as the markings of a common gene pool, split apart into new and isolated strands carried by the tribes. 
Said isolation, alongside constant interracial conflict and assumed increased rates of inbreeding, may explain the perceived cognitive and linguistic degeneration of the Drak.

Cultural and linguistic degeneration: 
The Drak texts recovered from more recent layers of sediment — often dredged from coastal waters or shipwrecks — tend to exhibit simpler structures, reduced vocabulary, and degraded syntax when compared to earlier samples unearthed in local temples. This suggests a loss of linguistic complexity over time.

It appears that the trajectory of their societal evolution may have stagnated — or even regressed. Additionally, if I interpret correctly, it is to be assumed that they hold a grudge or a somewhat natural aversion to technological advancements and engineering. They perceive most modern human inventions as admissions of weakness rather than solutions. Further research is required.

3628.title: Drak — Tribal Structure
3628.text:
Upon examining these Drak inscriptions, my analysis is as follows:

Tribal Structure:

The Drak hardly consider themselves as a unified species or culture, instead preferring increasingly insular and tribal groupings despite sharing a common language root and build.
Over the course of generations, these divisions have led to distinct scale patterns, color morphologies, dialectical shifts, and unique cultural practices — notably, a preference for different holy idols/ sages/ war heroes that shape their understanding of self, and are titular to their tribal variation.
Tribes lay claim to different domains geographically, locked in an interracial territorial conflict whenever the brood's expansion demands it.

The Drak'Dal, for example, are named for their idol, Dalszul, and currently contest the archipelago offshore alongside the Drak'Mer; followers of Merphisz. This conflict has seemingly begun after the Drak'Dal were driven out of the Veilwater Basin. 

Other notable tribes include:
Drak'Ari, followers of Arisztar
Drak'Fyr, followers of Fyraszh

3629.title: A Doctor Turned Coroner
3629.text:
We had long run out of any meaningful medicine when we captured the injured Ancient. There was nothing that I could have done for it, even if I had wanted to.

Stitching up the walking, bloated corpses around me had used up every bandage. Suturing their ruptured organs shut — or in place — had cost us all thread. For me to dull the thrumming of my own head, well, I had emptied every Elixer flask I'd brought.

So as the Ancient lay dying, all I could do was watch. So watch I did, as it crumbled betwixt my fingers, turned gray, and fell to ash.

It was so peculiar.
When you lose patients — human ones — you close their eyes, bury their bodies, and visit their overgrown graves once or twice. 
But when an Ancient dies, it fades from the world. After an eternity on Embervale, all they leave is dust. There is nothing to bury, really. Nothing to mourn.

My head's pounding again. Should've brought more Elixir...

3630.title: Field Notes — Day 8 of Yearwake, 509 D.A.
3630.text:
Rimgard's soldiers are good for one thing, at least. After they broke through the Ancient barrier, I was able to slip past.  If they could break the seal here, they most likely managed to surmount the gate, as well...

Lord Vorgoth must already be on his way. Right now, it's just a thesis... but not without circumstantial evidence:
The Shroud has gathered here in unprecedented levels. It creeps from the Veilwater Basin all the way through to... where, exactly? Some central point, a platform I can spy far below.... right beneath the floating isles. 

I am not alone in my quest to ascend. Rotting tendrils stretch upward, clawing at the 
drifting land rafts above — keeping them low. And therefore, within even my reach.

As long as the Shroud's attention is away from this platform, there may still be time. I have to take my chances.

— Loraine Crim

3631.title: Of Thyme And Tenderness
3631.text:
I thought of my old beliefs as a coat I could shed.
Now, I realize they've tainted me in a way that was so far beyond my comprehension. They've seeped into my body, lingering just beneath the skin.

When I began my journey here, I did so with the best intentions. To better understand the Ancients. To learn and to grow.
And still,  I came with weaponry. Swords, bows, daggers — I wanted to be prepared. Prepared for anything. For battle.

That's why I gripped my wand tightly when I saw the Ancient in the distance. It was the first time that I ever laid eyes on one of their kind. They rose from a grassy patch in the valley, suddenly tall against the setting sun. Then, the arched back down. 
They were sampling thyme. And humming.

I felt shame wash over me as I loosened my grip. My instincts had betrayed me yet again. So for a time, I just stood there. Listening to a melody that sounded familiar, as if it were human... and maybe it was. Perhaps even more so than I.

From now on, I'll continue without my weapons, without fear, and with a new tune on my lips to march to. Some notes come out crooked; others choke me still... Yet, it's not the song that plagues me, but the horrid cough that rattles below. 

Darya

3632.title: Report: Plant Seed Vault
3632.text:
The new seed storage sector is coming to fruition. Once completed, the conservatory will have the capacity to preserve genetic material for secondary — and potentially tertiary — ecological projects, expanding the scope of future restorative or evolutionary initiatives.

Near endless possibilities are blossoming before us... No pun intended. Yet, I find our side projects most riveting. The ongoing development of the Fig'23 flavor profile presents several promising avenues for culinary use.
Through cultivating a mutated strand, we can make the fruit prickly, sour, and sweet on the tongue. I'm thinking of calling it "Prickle Pearl". 

Each discovery opens another path for exploration, but while there is much we know, there's far more we don't. The work continues.

Elder Claravinta

3633.title: Our Gods Have Risen
3633.text:
Our gods have risen. They chose lava earth for their kingdom and lifted their temples into the sky.
Would be easier for Drak'Fyr on volcanic ground. Easy for Drak'Ari drifting through sky. But we are Drak'Dal. We come from the ground.
There has to be reason this great challenge is ours. The final trial has begun.
We are worthy. We will succeed. Human demise is settled.

3634.title: Observatory Report
3634.text:
My findings on the Andromeda's Eye telescope are as follows:

Objective Lens, Star Diagonal, Eyepiece - Working as intended.

Optical Tube Assembly - Working as intended, but dusty. Should we send a student to aid in cleaning...?

Mount - Error detected. The Telescope does not move horizontally or perpendicularly. 

Focusing Components - Working as intended, though they cause me great misery nevertheless — Seeing as they can only reveal the constellations directly up ahead.

Conclusion: Consider conducting a proper maintenance routine.

- Professor Androme

3635.title: The Full Moon Brings Clarity
3635.text:
Two heartbeats rattle my ribcage.

One clings to a vengeful rhythm. It expands, rips and tears, suffocates me from within. It feels righteous, though vindictive.

There is another tone that reverberates inside. A quiet hum, mild with remembrance of... of what, exactly? Some spectre of myself I do not recognize; less wizened and haggard.

He speaks of a border that can only be ruled by a strong hand. Of a proud but shattered kingdom, wishing to unite — held together in a fist. Of a seed of secrecy, a threat, planted in the outer rind of his brain and nurtured until rootbound.

He is the Guard of the North
The warden of the wall
And he, too, is crushed under the fist

For he lives in a world of mice and men, where the cowards tether one below
Where one needs a sword to sever these ties that bind
Ties that cannot be remade
Where the weak are culled, and one must rise to live
So the walls must be taller, and the ascent higher
and the distance grows forever, until everything below is misty blue

The mist unites, so says the seed
In the Shroud, everything is whole, and all is one, and one is all
And so the right hand stretched out to deliver what it carries
A fist; a sword; an end
A cerulean thread to stitch two hearts as one

— Lord Vorgoth, Guard of the North, Ruler of Rimgard

3636.title: Operations Overview
3636.text:
The site handles the extraction of raw minerals and metals from the surrounding deposits. Once pulled, material is sorted and loaded at the transport station for shipment to processing locations elsewhere. Flow has been steady — no major holdups.

Left-over building blocks from our tower restoration are being held in the storage area adjacent to the mining site for now. It keeps them close to transit and out of the way of active extraction.

3637.title: A New Era
3637.text:
Both recharge stations and model rigs are in order, though the terminal seems uncharacteristically untidy and crowded — but I suppose the residents tend more to the greenhouse than to construct maintenance. 
Elder Claravinta really only focuses on whatever occupies her mind most. It's very "human" of her, I fear.

That reminds me: Recent proximity to humanity has inspired me to come up with a new invention! A model suit, meant to combine my construct research with the agile, human frame — bipedal, and somewhat compressed to fit the strange proportions these stubby animals possess.

Perhaps this venture will one day bring forth a new era for our constructs, or the Ancients at large! I'd be most interested in shaping the 4th generation of models... but I must not get ahead of myself! For now, it's best I continue my journey to the Worker's Ward. I hear there is another site nearby that requires a routine check-up.

- Artificer Constantio

3638.title: Elder Claravinta's Notes, Entry 2
3638.text:
We suffer from stagnation.
A new flavor, I admit — though a bittersweet one at best.

We don't possess enough energy to fuel our ascent. 

Therefore, we remain in the interim; suspended above the grime and dirt — reaching for the fruit of the stars, hands bound.

We are ripped apart. And as such, we will remain.
Corporally, spiritually...

When we are only half, then we are not enough.

Maybe we will never be.

3639.title: Assembly Record — 391st Council Proceedings
3639.text:
Members Present
Listed in order of seniority: Manathor, Eldermere, Claravinta, Ezramin.

Topic 1: Ecological Impact of Botanical Alteration

Ongoing alterations to the composition of local flora have demonstrated additional effects on wildlife populations.

Motion:
That all botanical research activities be suspended.

Vote:
Unanimous opposition. Motion denied.

Notes:
Elder Claravinta proposed limiting future experimentation to controlled greenhouse environments to minimize unintended ecological impact.

Topic 2: Observatory Operations and Resource Allocation

Work in the observatory continues, but progress has plateaued.

Motion:
That additional resources be allocated to interstellar charting efforts to better identify viable routes.

Vote:
Unanimous approval. Motion carried.

Notes:
None.

Topic 3: Human Contact with the Elixir
Humanity has discovered the Elixir. How this came about remains unknown. Consequences are expected to be unfavorable.

Motion:
That the council maintains noninterference.

Vote:
Inconclusive. Deliberation postponed.

Notes:
This constitutes the first inconclusive vote recorded in recent council history.
Council member Ezramin expressed strong opposition during proceedings and was subsequently asked to withdraw from the chamber.

3640.title: Snow Or Cinders
3640.text:
The gateway to the Albaneve Summits research lab is finished.

This may well be by far the least favored biosphere... the freezing air makes it difficult to draw from any fire; any energy around. I much prefer the calming heat of the Cradle. It's simply so invigorating!

Humanity seems to avoid the cold, too — though some also revel in its briskness, and the challenge those lonely mountains in particular provide. 
Most curious. There may be a hidden charm to the snow that I have not yet discovered. Perhaps constructing a snowpal would aid me in my quest of understanding!

3641.title: Mermaid Eyes
3641.text:
There was once a mermaid
Below the mirror of the moon
In crystal puddles, she'd wait
'Fore hunger'd wake her soon

Something gnawed at her inside
The thirst, a thrill to seek
A sanguine flush lit up her eyes
She sought something to eat.

Floral scent on her skin
Smile rosé like wine
She'd draw someone in
A partner to dine 

They thought her heart pure
Saw the sparkle in her gaze
Had fallen for her lure
Suffocation, sweet embrace

So the water's red, gushing
For her dance inspires
The moon to start blushing
From the blood of admirers

3642.title: Final Report: Greenhouse Development
3642.text:
I present herewith my findings on our cultivation project, prepared in accordance with the Council's decree.

My observations can be summarized as follows:

The ferns exhibit healthy growth and development, continuing to improve overall air quality. Efforts to increase the climate resilience of Bloomhearts through the implementation of a protective petal overcoat have borne fruit — No jest intended.

Analysis of the latest harvest indicates no significant reduction in quality. The fruit's flavor profile remains consistent with that of earlier specimens.

Based on these findings, the project can be considered a success. Continued observation is recommended to assess long-term stability and performance.

Capacity remains limited. We may consider moving further experimentation efforts to our post in the Revelwood.

Elder Claravinta

3643.title: Elder Claravinta's Notes, Entry 1
3643.text:
The council may be divided, but it matters not. We must ascend. There is no other choice.

It seems our youngest member plans to leave the council.
To split from both the council and the Mother Flame's embrace at one's own behest is, of course, an ignominy — and even worse: entirely witless.

As soon as Ezramin departs, we will count the votes anew — and the outcome will be clear as day. Then, we will route our energy to the Mother Flame to fuel our ascent... but whether or not it will be enough, none can say.

3644.title: Field Notes — Day 26 of Yearwake, 509 D.A.
3644.text:
I've felt this heat before. 

Long ago, I left my assistant Nala to research a monument within the Pillars of Creation... a strange, portal-like structure amid a sea of flame.
She called it a "gateway"— a jest, I know. And yet: Perhaps she was right. And perhaps... this platform could be similar: A teleporter to the isles above.

Of course, it's not activated. That would be too easy, wouldn't it?
Two observations:
1. I see pillars of light in the distance, aligned with the directions of the markers that surround the platform.

2. These pillars may be akin to the beacons of the Ancient Spires, and must be conquered to power the teleporter! 

...Let's add a third remark, for good measure:
3. My provisions are running low. I cannot, should not leave this platform. 

I wonder what Nala or Fran would say if they could see me now: On the other side of the world, the edge of eternity, reaching for the stars while being chained to a pit.

It seems I only learnt the language of the Ancients to understand a single, cruel joke. In fact, I may have become the punchline.

Well, we'll see who gets the last laugh. I still have hope. I always will.

3645.title: First At The Top
3645.text:
Mushy humans found a way through barrier. They think they better than us. Not again. We went in just behind them. 
We dig. We mine. Every chunk of metal we tear from this rock is a blade, a shield, a dent in a mushy skull.
We take what should be ours.

They were first at the gate, 
we will be first at the top!

3646.title: Close To The Clouds Above
3646.text:
Destiny draws near. Their cursed Citadel is closer than ever... and within it, their weapon. The fire which we ought to snuff out... The Mother Flame, which threatens to burn us alive. The source of their infinity, and lifeblood of their kind.

We must separate the mice from the men
The rats from the rulers
The Ancients from the ashes of rebirth

We must douse her. To unite everything. To become whole, so the Wanderer says.

He stood by my side, one step from the edge, arms stretched out wide.
"This is what the birds see." He said. "The birds of prey. High, far up above the rest... floating."

Why, yes. I should float. Above the rats. Above all. 
This is where I was meant to be from the beginning, and where I'm meant to bring forth the end. Though my heart aches... I will fulfill my duty.

— Lord Vorgoth, Guard of the North, Ruler of Rimgard

3647.title: Silly Fishies
3647.text:
Stupid, stupid fishies!

Always flee Kra'Tau's arrows! Rah!
Think they can outsmart Kra'Tau? Think again!

Kra'Tau throw bow into pond. Useless! No one need coward weapon like that! Kra'Tau catch fishies with claws, then stomp with feet. Make fish soup the old-fashioned way!

Then silly fishies no laugh at Kra'Tau missing shots! Fishies won't laugh at all no more —  fishies stomped dead!!

Rah rah!

3648.title: My Notes Are Safe
3648.text:
I loathe abandoning this project before completion, but the elders are right. Gems simply do not possess enough energy to power our ascent.

Still, I may return to my forge blueprints eventually... so I've stored my notes away on the upper floor.

It seems the lock mechanism is working as intended. Being able  to see the door and the light above it from the button below is really quite practical!

3649.title: Into The Flame
3649.text:
We tried to rise. To escape. To save ourselves — to save the Mother Flame. But we are stuck. Something's got a hold of us, and we all know too well what it is.
The plan now is to go into the flame. That is all we have left. And the others – they are grabbing things. Their most prized possessions. I don't know what they think will come out of it. Maybe they don't know either. But their panic is spreading and I feel it now too.
The only thing I have left of real value are the full golden building blocks. They're much too heavy. I have to leave them behind and just hope.
I am going in as I am. Knowledge is the only thing worth carrying anyway. Everything else is just weight.

(But just in case, I hid them close by but out of sight. So when I come back, something is waiting for me)

3650.title: Gem Forges: Construction Notes, Generation VII
3650.text:
Primary Materials:
Effusion Rock: High silicon content required. Preferred substrate: Basalt (for adequate thermal stability)
Precious Metal Conduit: Aurum alloy recommended. (superior conductivity and resistance to arcane deterioration.)

Inner Fibre Hull: Candidate materials under review:
Celestium:  Increases structural integrity and energy retention.
Moonstone: Too brittle for compression. However, adularescence may improve internal light propagation. Further testing required.

Conductor Assembly:
Use diamond lattices for maximum durability and better resistance to internal fractures.

Foundation Base:
Construct a wide circular base to ensure uniform pressure distribution across forge chamber flooring. 

Compression:
Reinforce overhead supports to prevent structural distortion.

Final Reminder:
Increase storage capacity for Archaic Essences. Insufficient containment may result in uncontrolled combustion.

3651.title: Construct Report, No. 34
3651.text:
Construct rigs were exchanged successfully. The Worker's Ward is now fully equipped with 3rd-generation models. Please find additional information attached below.

Worker Constructs
M.I.N.R.
The new Metallurgical, Industrial, and Nonmetal extraction Rigs have elevated efficiency by about 34%. This productivity increase is largely attributable to the Archaic Core additions, which enable new models to recharge at Charge Stations.

G.T.H.R.
New Grunts (Transportation and Hauling Rigs) were deployed. The process of gathering, transporting, and storing sediment and ore has been streamlined.

C.R.T.R.
The Construct Reconstruction and Termination Rigs were deployed for improved rig maintenance.

Results are satisfactory. Implementation approved.
Seeing as this report is finished, I'll withdraw to my chambers once more to conclude my own research — please do not disturb me. The entry is concealed for a reason.

- Artificer Constantio

3652.title: Imbued With Magic
3652.text:
The constructs are simple, straightforward creations with linear purpose and ability. The MINR drones deployed here, for example, were equipped with diamond-tipped drills. This enables them to operate, when used in tandem with Charge Stations, nearly indefinitely.

Despite their efficacy, they're dull. Mindless husks fueled by an unrelenting flow of energy, and entirely interchangeable.

We Ancients are different. Our souls, gifts from the Flame, hold our minds. They are finite and delicate, carefully granted to our similarly "constructed" bodies in Proto Vessels. The corpus serves as a shell that contains the spark, imbuing us with warmth and light.

I find these connections between "body/mind" or "mechanical/ephemeral" most fascinating, but I wonder... could the power of the Flame grant ability, even if it were inverted? 

The answer I discovered is this Eternal Ice Arrow — but the coldness it exudes is deeply unpleasant to me, so I may set it aside for now.

3653.title: Elder Claravinta's Notes, Entry 3
3653.text:
We've no more fuel to burn, and the Shroud has reached our abode.
We could not run. Could not hide. We were a harvest, ripe for picking.

For the first time in centuries, an Ancient has died by the blade — severed from the Mother Flame's light... trying desperately to stall the worms, the tendrils, the rot.

A fruitless venture, of course. 

We should not die as shields. We should die as fuel... to buy time. To flee. To save what matters most.
We will be the energy — until our bodies can be reshaped, until our souls are reborn... if ever.
There is no other way.

3654.title: Air Current Network
3654.text:
To improve traversal between the smaller splitter islands, we have begun establishing a series of directed air currents — stable upstreams intended to serve as fixed transit corridors across the Ancient Land.
Navigation along these routes is aided considerably by the Signal Blocks, which emit a strong enough light to remain visible at great distance, including low-visibility conditions such as overcast weather or night time. They function well as orientation markers.
Additional Signal Blocks are stored on an island beyond our current range. The air currents are not yet calibrated to support passage that far out.

3655.title: Many Changes, New Challenges
3655.text:
My ascent was successful, though I must admit our newly rifted environs have greatly hindered me on the journey. No matter — I deem this site adequate for storing and preparing the constructs designated to work at the nearby ward. 
The local tower is a pleasant architectural addition that can double as a safe for valuables, should an alarm arise.

Furthermore, I've progressed on my research with the construct suit. The skewed proportions really do appear charming to me. Humans are just so compact, aren't they? 
For an alpha version, it will most definitely suffice. Perhaps the construct hub at Manathor's Plaza will provide me with even more inspiration. I'm slated to head there next.

- Artificer Constantio

3656.title: The End Approaches
3656.text:
Vorgoth is coming, and he's bringing his army.

The barrier, already weakened from our energy redistribution and ascent, has been breached.
We cannot run — we have to rise before it's too late!

The sky is our only escape... Only there can the Mother Flame be safe!

It has to work. It simply must...

3657.title: Legends Of The Ruined Knight
3657.text:
John told me another of his stories yesterday. Seems like all the booze we shared had loosened his lips and fueled his imagination. I didn't mind... the night was humid and ripe for mystery.
He leaned in, hushing as if sharing a secret... I felt his breath on my ear. My head was buzzing from the ale, but I made sure to listen closely.

Once upon a time, there was a valiant knight who was brought to ruin by the curse of the Flame.
Despite his downfall, the knight sought not revenge, but repentance. Determined to atone, he wandered the edge of Embervale to reach the old Sky Port — his only path towards finding forgiveness beyond. 

Yet, when the harbor of winds broke down, so did his spirit. His only chance at redemption was whisked away. Devastated, he knelt atop a mountain and gazed at the Port from afar, waiting... until he faded. 
The knight wants something he can never have. I understand his heartache all too well... hanging onto a promise, a whisper of hope... 
I still feel John's words on my skin. It's just a fairy tale, I tell myself... but its sweet allure brings me back to him every time.

3658.title: Strange Human Customs
3658.text:
Humans have hair. Not a single strand, of course, nor matted long coats of fur — no! They have tufts of it, mostly (but not exclusively!) atop their slightly oblong marble heads.

It can be long, short, curly, straight, blond, red, pitch black, and so many other curious things! Some are blessed with very healthy, youthful manes, while others must prematurely kiss their locks goodbye — revealing said glistening egglike domes. In conclusion, there are as many facets of hair as there are humans themselves!

I find this incredibly fascinating... but if the others discover my juvenile interests, they may send me back to the Mother Flame immediately!

What to do, what to do...

3659.title: The Circle's Origin
3659.text:
Once upon a time, the Mother Flame produced a spark every solstice. Now, we are lucky to receive "offspring" once a decade. Our numbers have dwindled ever since our youngest began to meddle with humanity.

This is most shameful. A mark on our pride and neutrality.
To waste one's life — to leave the circle, to forsake the mother's embrace in the name of something so laughable as empathy... is pitiful. 

But still, I must admit... As the eldest, I can feel the Mother Flame's pull, but uncertainty plagues me, so I, too, refuse her call.

Because it hasn't always been like this, has it?
The voices in the Flame, echoes through space and time, speak of fathers. Brothers. Sons. Of families and origins that were unbound, unrenewable... but their whispers all bleed together, chained as one. 

We used to be born. We used to die. We used to be remembered.
So, how calcified is our journey? How forgettable, how memorable may I be?
...And how wrong, how true, how unchangeable are we, really?

- Manathor

3660.title: More Connected Than Divided
3660.text:
Humans have flames, as do we. 
They use fire to forge bonds, to light the dark, and to destroy. It can be summarized as the source of all their inventions; all their progress. Our Flame is not so unlike theirs.

Humans eat fruit and drink wine, as do we.
In fact, we've only adopted these customs due to humanity's influence — a factor often forgotten all too willingly.

Humans gaze at the stars, as do we.
We are all under the same skies. The same constellations. They've shown us their suspicion and wrath, but also their tremendous kindness — especially the people of Orindell.

Are we so different after all? Ought we to preserve a kind of hollow sanctity, only because we are hundreds, and they are millions? Because we lay claim to endlessness? I think not. I think we share more than we care to admit. And shouldn't that mean that we ought to stand beside them, rather than judge from above?

Embervale belongs to all of us.
- Ezramin

3661.title: The End
3661.text:
We have to abandon all our efforts.
Every construct. Every spire. Every proto vessel. Yes, even my own creations.

A new arrival was due this solstice. The proto vessels were ready. We were ready. It is a pity. No, it is shameful. I always enjoyed welcoming a young Ancient. A new face, an old soul... sometimes, I thought I could see those that came before inside their spark. Remnants of previous lives, like leftover mechanisms from retired construct models.

Our numbers may grow no further. Perhaps we are doomed to be diminished after all. I cannot bend the solstice, nor the Shroud — but I can store whatever I have for those who follow after me. 
I've hidden the final piece of my construct suit in this room, behind a loose stone in the walls of a nook. Perhaps it will aid you, whoever you are. And then, maybe, there will still be hope for us.

- Artificer Constantio

3662.title: Ancients aren't born. We are salvaged.
3662.text:
The Mother Flame grants us life. She lets us walk the Earth in search of wisdom and discovery — and when we return to her, carrying our gifts, she takes it back. For a time, at least.

Therefore, Ancient souls, or sparks, are limited. They linger in the light, connected to all that came before, and all that will ever be, until expelled anew — wiped clean. 

This cycle is holy. Its purity is beyond reproach. 

But a spark alone cannot be. It is merely a consciousness, a soul, a memory core in need of a host. To house a spark, we require a shell. Shells are disposable. They crumble to dust as our end draws near, not meant to be mourned.

Should we perish outside the Flame's grasp — an unlikely event, as we reign eternal — then we are lost, until returned to her light.

- Manathor

3663.title: Dire Times
3663.text:
The terminal is in perfect condition. Elevators, lights, and recharge stations all seem in order.

Constructs are maintained in the basement, where repairs and security details are handled. Once ready, they're deployed to the middle floor via lift. The lift continues upward, capable of carrying controller personnel to the command center above.

Everything is clean and tidy. I suppose the landfill — or gaping abyss — below the basement is used frequently to declutter. 
My plan was to stay longer and retrieve some materials for my construct suit, but my time here has been cut short. The Mother Flame calls upon all Ancients to gather in the citadel.
I reckon that this is due to the encroaching Shroud... but I cannot be certain.

No matter what, I will ensure to pass through the Proto Vessel Bay on my path. The future — our future — must be preserved!

- Artificer Constantio

3664.title: And They May Never Heal
3664.text:
Manathor is gone. Faded, somewhere at world's end... moments before the final reckoning.
The fleeting, the wild brutes, the cursed, the bloodthirsty. The wise, both the embraced, and the lost...
In the end, it did not matter who or what you were — what we were.

All were swallowed. And all will be gone.
A dark void to take in all light; to blacken the skies... the shadows fall on us the same.

And it always will.
Over, and over, and over... unless we strike at the root.

3665.title: The Flame
3665.text: The realm has fallen, consumed by the Shroud. The old world lies in ruin. You have been awakened by the enduring Flame. There is much to learn, child. Go forth.

3666.title: Ode To Pikemead
3666.text:
Gather 'round, we're drinkin'! An ode to the Queen, once young! 
3 babes on 'er arm, cup filled to the brim
Thinkin' out loud, she'd sung: 

Rather mead in my cup, 
or my cup filled with rum
drink too much,
rather than be done!

Can't only have some,
So share some around,
drink too much,
rather than drink one!

Rather mead in my head,
and my head on the run
Than my head on a pike
with none!

Get the rum, and the mead
Get the mead, in the cup
Get the cup to your head
drink up!

3667.title: Glorious Seeds!
3667.text:
This fascinating seed I bought — It takes root and sprouts fast! I find myself dreaming of it at night — the faint glow, illuminating my garden and my soul. I must plant more. The whole village should learn of its glory!

— Hemming, Yearwake, 502 D.A.

3668.title: It's No Use
3668.text:
Aunt Gertrude won't budge. She wants to stay at the home where she and my mother grew up. It doesn't matter that the town's dead, that everyone's gone, that she's all alone... She wants to live and die there. What a sad, old woman... she'd rather be with her bundle of strays than with the rest of her family! 

I can't stand those dogs she lets into her house. They're always pregnant and full of fleas, like that "Pompom" she loves. I'm giving up. Tell your children not to wander to Shorewatch, or they might catch rabies! Or worse, fleas!

3669.title: As We All Forget
3669.text:
I so fondly recall my clueless years, foolishly venturing further than the rest. The depths piqued my interest, full of wonder and awe. I reached out, yearning for knowledge, veiled in the warmth of the Flame. I was young and feared no mistakes. In the abyss, I felt eternity.

I feel it no more. The sand in my hourglass slips away. When I hear the Flame call the name of the eldest — my name — I am filled with regret. Our planet's core has changed... the ripple effect of my discoveries tore the valleys and our youngest apart. Failure should have scared me, not change. The abyss is all that remains, and it means oblivion.
I've branded my name into the stone — recorded all my failures on the Obelisks, burdened to outlast me. Fearing to be forgotten, I signed my name on the last... how very human of me. Curious, this final feeling. So hollow. So cold. 

— Manathor

3670.title: Turquoise Waters
3670.text:
Turquoise waters glisten, golden sands
A dreamlike oasis stretches across the lands
Endless blue with crystal-clear skies
Air rich with warmth since sunrise

Turquoise depths that sparkle and gleam,
A liquid mirror, a living dream
Waves roll gently, soft as the breeze,
An ocean of blue with perfect ease

3671.title: A New Mystery Unfolds
3671.text:
They are more than legends after all. 
The Hollow Halls exist, and inside them echo the melodies of a bygone age... memories of a time where clear skies reigned, and the Shroud was still slumbering below.

These Halls of unknown origin have existed for millennia, but their architecture differs from that of the Ancients. Most curious. 

It's said that these crypts served as banishment grounds for the lowest of Embervale. I wonder if the cursed inhabitants still walk this earthly plane...

- Balthazar

3672.title: My Dearest Helên
3672.text:
Please hold your tears and sit by my side. Let us gaze over the valley, as we've done before. The setting sun and falling leaves are like our brief and precious time. Let us share these hours before the Shroud whisks them away.

Come rest your head on my shoulder, my daffodil.

Yours forever,
Salim

3673.title: CURSE THESE NUMBSKULLS
3673.text:
They nigh blew me to smithereens, those scoundrels!

"Dieter, go witness! We discovered a chest in the new tunnel, I swear it! Nay, Dieter, 'tis no jest, observe for yourself!"

My mouth is choked with dust, and my hands are numb from digging! My nails splinter... I am famished.

Vicious curs! May the Shroud take you all!

3674.title: He'll Be Fine Down There!
3674.text:
Dieter fares well, cease your prattle! He has shovel and fortitude, he'll be out of the mineshaft shortly. Perhaps he plays a prank on us, that scamp.

Pray tell, did you put some provisions in there, Hans..?

All the same, he'll survive.

Aye, the chest was fine bait... though we had some need of it... fie, should have considered this before...

3675.title: Falling To Ruin
3675.text:
We held out hope, digging through the rubble, our lips whispering prayers to the Ancients. Always a watchful eye towards the horizon. Even in this furthest corner of the world, the Shroud threatens to engulf us and seal away any ray of hope.

As the air grew thick with that cursed fog, we held on. As fires raged on the horizon, ash falling like snow on Howling Peak, we pushed harder. 

May this home, long kept, usher us into a brighter age.

513 D.A.

3676.title: Careful With This Shipment!
3676.text:
Argon,

Take care with this new shipment from the valley. The Merchant said it is highly volatile. Apparently, the "explosives explode"  if jostled or tossed about. Who would have known? 

Anyway, I paid a pretty penny for this. DO NOT mess around in here. I can't afford to fix another hole in the wall!

3677.title: A Good Night's Rest
3677.text:
Finally, a break from the tedious work. My bones are sore... but some shelter, the warmth of a fire, and comfort should allow me to gather new energy. 

This old cot isn't the softest, but it'll do. I'll get some shut-eye here until I'm rested — ready and full of stamina for another sunrise. I hope I'll have sweet dreams despite the hunger...

Food is getting scarce... I hear they're planning an expedition. Thankfully, I hid some rations behind my bed. They will make for a nice meal when cooked over fire.

3678.title: Don't Leave My Side!
3678.text:
Jezmina, is it true? The Ancients call upon you to stay behind as the rest of us slumber? Will you be there when I awake? Please, you cannot leave my side! You're my all! 

Why must we change? I miss the old days when we used to travel... together, side by side. You let me linger next to you. You held my hand. And now? All this secrecy, for what? I thought you could confide in me. I don't want the Ancients to drive us apart! I'll lose all faith!

If you must go, at least give me a farewell kiss.

All my heart,
— Emily

3679.title: Captain's Journal, Day One of Midyear, 512 D.A.
3679.text:
"Hold the chamber to your last breath." These were the words of the Ancient one, before he entered with a handful of our best warriors. It was the first time I'd seen one of his kind, and I expect it will be the last. His face is burned in my mind. My life, and those of my remaining soldiers, are pledged to this sacred duty. 
— Captain Arkwright

3680.title: The Shroud Looms
3680.text:
The bluejays no longer drift so carelessly through the air. Something is changing. 

A nebula flows towards us, springs from the abyss like a tidal wave. They call it the Shroud. It carries disease and suffering, changes soil and people.

I must understand this madness, but discovering a remedy may prove difficult. Many trade routes between kingdoms have ceased operation... it seems that both materials and trust are in low supply.

— Balthazar, 500 D.A.

3681.title: War
3681.text:
They took Pikemead's Reach. They killed King Gormander.
An army of lunatics, sickly pale, barely lifting their feet above the bloodied ground. They drag themselves through our valleys, through the miasma, led by the mad Guard of the North, Lord Vorgoth of Rimgard. I always knew the Elixir would sow a seed of distrust.

I look up at the Ancient Spires, at the sky... There is no running, no hiding. We must persevere.

— Balthazar, 503 D.A.

3682.title: On The Flame And Its Murmurs
3682.text:
Pure light engulfs the knowledge of the ancient breed, protects it in a flaming core. Wisdom far beyond my own imagination. I could stare into the fire for hours, seeking answers, a whisper... But I hear none. Despite possessing a voice, it only speaks to those born from the Flame.

A shame, as I believe we could have quite enlightened conversations.
— Balthazar, 508 D.A.

3683.title: Working Overtime
3683.text:
We had to fill the carts with at least 6 pounds of salt for Saline Springs, so I was pulling extra hours after the sun had gone down.

I went through the motions with a blank mind when my pickaxe suddenly struck something solid. As I pulled to loosen my tool, a large stone chunk was brought forth into the lantern's dim glow. The relief looked different from the shimmering salt surrounding it, but I could barely make it out in the low light. Squinting, I tried to focus on the shape. Nestled inside a lap of rubble sat a near-spherical object. 
I commanded my tired eyes to follow the swirling lines that drew toward its center, but became ever more drowsy. When I reached out to trace it, I felt a sharp pain in my shoulder. How long had I been digging? I decided to rest.

It took some time to heal up. In my absence, they've opened a new mineshaft and boarded up the old one. Maybe it's for the better. We can't be distracted when there's a quota to meet.

3684.title: Smothered And Devoured By Obscurity
3684.text:
The Shroud swallows all, even us. We become lost to dusk, vanish, and morph into a sea of cornflower-stained twilight. 
Never have I encountered a sickness, a curse of this gravitas. The fog burns eyes and lungs, but doesn't quite kill. It spreads. It manipulates. It eats away at us, slowly, leaving only a husk.

Even the Ancients have become ephemeral in the face of this malady. Their capital, a city far beyond reach and comprehension, has ascended above the clouds... an act of dereliction, or desperation?

There is no cure for this. Only the power of the Flame can keep the Shroud at bay. 

— Balthazar, 505 D.A.

3685.title: Elusive Purple
3685.text:
I've been wandering the lands, fascinated by the rich and vibrant purples that nature so effortlessly weaves into petal and berry. Such depth, such brilliance — I must seize it for myself. I have boiled roots and crushed blossoms, mixed minerals and whispered spells, yet the color eludes me. The shade slips through my fingers like mist at dawn.

But I will not rest. Somewhere in earth or essence, the secret awaits. And when I seize it, it shall be more than mere pigment. It shall be power, beauty, and fortune itself.

3686.title: These Lands
3686.text:
"Morwenna" would be as quiet and peaceful as my late aunt, I imagine... if it weren't for those pests!

They gnaw at everything I build! From barn to edifice, monument to manor... ripped to shreds by wild beasts! It's as if they're laughing at my artistry! 

They weren't always so ferocious. Forced to leave their natural habitats, maybe? Is it this spreading blight people whisper about? Aunt Irvetta says they seem "scared" more than anything. Back then, I couldn't see her point... which she blamed on my one remaining eye. I did not find this jest to be funny.

I planned to name a town after you, too, dear Irvetta. Once. Now, perhaps I'd consider a village. Maybe a hamlet. Or a hovel. 
You're my least favorite aunt for a reason, Irvetta!

Cade Hawthorn, 500 D.A.

3687.title: My Flame-touched Friend
3687.text:
First, you were my savior. The other kids laughed at me when I couldn't read or write. You pushed them into the dirt, laughing back, and read me tales until I learned the words. You were smarter and braver.

Later, you were my love. Holding hands by the riverbed, I confessed. You broke my heart, fiery whirlwind you are. I forgave you. How could I not? At least you were honest with me.

Now, what are you? A hollowed-out husk, burnt up by anger. There's nothing left of the woman I once held dear. 
In the end, I told you not to do it. But you never listen, do you?

3688.title: Strength Of The Vukah
3688.text:
This arena belongs to a warrior clan defined by violent conquest. They gather on this hillside to wage gladiator battles where the lone survivor is crowned — what I've come to call The Brawler. 

Despite sharing voracity, these Vukah conduct different rites from the ones who've overtaken Fort Kelvin. While their rituals of sacrifice may diverge, blood spilled is blood gained in the eyes of their deities: 
Proto-beasts that reign over earth and sky, born of flesh and made eternal through totems — able to bless, and to damn.

Vukah... do your immolations seek to impress, or to appease? When you left your homes to haunt mine, was it to conquer, or to flee? What force of nature, what damnation, what faceless god brought you here?

I have to uncover your secrets, but inching closer would be certain death. Perhaps, when the Brawler lay sleeping... I could spy further.

Marianne Reed, 498 D.A.

3689.title: The Fearsome Dragon
3689.text:
I told them the truth, but they won't believe me! The dragon is real! 

I saw it while scavenging booze on the outer rims of our territory. When I stumbled into that cave and met its ferocious gaze, eyes glowing with mystical light — I turned 'round like a whirlwind and dashed off! 

The others spit and laugh at me! So what if I gulped down a little moonshine while out and about? I know what I saw!

3690.title: A Fearless Woman
3690.text:
You wouldn't believe the brawl you missed out on!! We watched the hounds battle it out when this woman — nay, this girl stomped into the arena, golden light reflecting on her armor plates, and raised her sword at the matron!
"I'm Gabrielle Fairburn" She said. "And if I beat you in a duel, you must leave this town and return it to its people!"

Of course, the matron accepted by spewing a massive fountain of bile at the girl! I thought I'd see her pale face melt away, but suddenly, a bright flash blinded me! Dancing light reflected from the girl as she ducked and dodged, and when the blindness faded, she was behind the matron, ready to strike!

Furiously, we jumped down from the rafters — against all of us, she stood no chance! Afterward, I pulled her body from the pool of sludge she lay in to drop her below. You should've seen her head hit the platform! Don't miss the next pit fight!

3691.title: Mind the "Nursery Supplies"
3691.text:
Elias —

Please note that the crates marked "Nursery Supplies" are indeed filled with weapons for the Contractor's rebel army. The guard is hot on our tail. I've buried the goods and marked the spot. Can't risk anything these days.

Several are packed with powerful explosives, so handle them with utmost care! We don't want to reveal our hiding spot! 

Keep quiet, yeah? We might lose our heads for this one!

— Benni

3692.title: A Note To Kendal
3692.text:
Sister! Have my notes reached you? I've missed you greatly this past year. That vile Contractor locked me up in a cellar on Jasper Isles, but your predictions came true: He couldn't keep me shackled for long! I'm so sorry I've been out of touch, but I've had to keep my head down... 

Umber Hollow isn't any better or worse than Surat's Rest. Two sides of the same coin, like us! More tavern brawls, perhaps — but nothing I can't handle!

The Nomad Highlands are without order. One day, Kendal, we must eclipse this chaos. What do you say?

Your sister,
Lupa

3693.title: Crimes Of Surat's Rest
3693.text:
Carlos! I received your note — and just in time, too. The patrols down here check every shipment thoroughly. The rumors of Umber Hollow you speak of are false — just yesterday we held a funeral for a young girl who was murdered up there in Surat's Rest! But I felt the same way when speaking with you in the market... intrigued to find a common, decent person amidst all the crimes committed where you are from. Everything from racketeering to corrupt courts and guards to widespread fraud. Perhaps we are both falling victim to decades of misspoken words. Are we not so alike, you and I?

Sincerely,
Emma

3694.title: Why Must I Waste Time As A Squire?
3694.text:
I know the Knight's Codex like the back of my hand. 
- Be "patient." Practice. Hard. Every damn day. 
- Master the basics of defense. Mind your downward sweep. Ensure the flick of your wrist is as fast as a flash.
- Care for your equipment, treat it as yet another limb, an extension of yourself. 

I know it all, off and on the battlefield. I can answer every question and every blow. My mind is a fortress, my defensive stance impenetrable.
Still, why does the mentor insist on locking me in the tower? Does he not see that I'm ready? Is it because I dodge more than I parry? Or because I polish my armor plate instead of the mentor's shoes?

I'm sick and tired of being patient! It's time I made my own rules:

- Be brave.
- Dodge beats block, block beats hit. Dance where others fall.
- Shine bright like the sun. Blind with valor and grace
... Return as a knight, or never.

Fairburn

3695.title: Alright Guys, This Isn't Funny
3695.text:
So you had a chuckle doodling on my face when I was knocked out. Very funny. You know what's not funny? 

I can't wash the paint off! I tried for hours to scrub your childish scribbles off me, but it's no use!
So all in all, great joke. Fantastic.

Wanna know the real punchline?
If I get my hands on the clown who did this, I'll rip his face off to use as my own.

I'll get the last laugh, I'll make sure of it!

3696.title: None Can Fool Me!
3696.text:
Thor came back from that scouting mission last night. He chucked this dusty bag with scrolls at me, and said it's the only thing they could scavenge. I know that fool well enough to see when he's lying through his teeth! 

My old friend pocketed a treasure for himself, but I won't rat him out. Instead, we'll gift that almanac to the matron as a tribute. 

And the treasure — well, Thor will have to share. Whatever he looted from Queen Jezmina's tent will be stashed away at his favorite spot, I reckon. After all this time, he still hasn't found a better hiding place than the top of that old watchtower.

3697.title: The Night Is Ruined!
3697.text:
Trust me, live music will be great for your tavern! No, we'd never cause trouble! Think of all the mead you'll sell with The Honeydews serenading your customers!

What a mess. That guy really had me wrapped around his little finger. I should've known that this band would cause trouble, they've such a bad reputation for stage fights, after all! But a live breakup? Come on, now!
And this bastard Miles even tried to get a room here after his band RUINED my establishment! I threw him out, but I swear I can still hear his stupid flute being played somewhere nearby. It's so damned grating. 

He does it to mock me while I pick up shattered plates and flip tables back around!

3698.title: The Band Is History
3698.text:
So that's it. My Honeydews are no more... We've split up many times, but something tells me last night was final. What's worse is that those bastards at the tavern wouldn't give me a room after my oh-so-kind bandmates — former bandmates, I suppose — made a mess of the place while fighting. Harper and Daniel never got along, but this was something else entirely. I should've tried to stop Harper from storming off towards that keep, but I was so busy dodging Dan's swings that I could hardly focus on anything else.

As it stands, I've got no band, no payment, and no bed. The bartender even insulted me. ME! Miles Rapore! Don't they know I'm a musical genius? Fools. In the morning, I'll set out again. Seems I needn't pack my flute. Perhaps I should give cobbling another try.

3699.title: Deserted
3699.text:
Sand fills my throat... my lungs grow heavy with dust. The storm still rages outside, whipping drifts to dunes, and dunes to dust devils. Oh, how I yearn to feel the cold again... The sapphire coast, windswept waves glistening in the sun... Children sharing sun-seared yucca in silk hammocks... torturous memories, too bright to hold close... my throat aches. 

Why did the Ancients forsake us after all...?

3700.title: Song Of Swooping Shadows
3700.text:
In a realm of tales untold,
Where shadows dance, mysteries unfold.
Flying creatures, strike from the sky,
Their warning shadows, swift and high.

Beware the darkened winged sprite,
Their presence brings a chilling fright.
Listen close to whispers old,
Secrets shared, their stories unfold.

Children, learn from ancient lore,
Guard your steps, forevermore.
In the land of dreams and wonder,
Heed the shadows, never blunder.

3701.title: My Little Pompom
3701.text:
I knew something was up when I picked her up last! My little girl, Pompom, is pregnant! 

I've set up a small, cozy space in my basement for her. She looks tired, but I trust everything will go well. I still remember when I took care of her mother, picking scrap metal from her spotted fur. Her family is hardy, and they've survived worse! With some luck, they'll even outlive little old me! 

I'll have to set out many more doggy bowls. I want them to be safe and sound long after I'm gone!

3702.title: I Must Protect The Weapon
3702.text:
When I first laid eyes on the reward the Mysterious Wanderer promised me, I was insulted. 
However, I quickly realized that this specter, this ghost who distorts reality as if I'm entering a dream, has bestowed me with a great gift... 

I hid the corrupted staff atop the wooden structure overlooking the Elixir distillery — only I deserve it. The visions of the floating figure still haunt me... I feel I might be dreaming, still.

3703.title: The Elixir, A Flood Of Woe
3703.text:
It's a formula I do not quite grasp, sophisticated beyond imagination. I'm not surprised to know that the source of this recipe is otherworldly.

Created from the flesh of these tiny, delicate fungi growing deep beneath the earth... It grants power. Yet, when I look at this flask, worry fills my heart. This will never be a cure. This will always be a weapon. Perhaps the Ancients hid this for a reason.

— Balthazar, 500 D.A.

3704.title: A Cold Reception, Yearfall, 506 D.A.
3704.text:
After a long and arduous journey, we've finally arrived at Rookmore. 

I'd hoped for a field hospital here, but instead, the only thing I found was tired faces, twisted by suspicion... I cannot blame them. The Kingdom of Meldore has many reasons to distrust Rimgard refugees, but the war affects us all, no matter the "side" we're on.

They won't hesitate for long. Everyone bleeds the same, whether it's at the bottom of a muddy trench or on a makeshift cot. I'll take matters into my own hands, as I did at the front, and set up camp in Woodgard. Once I can start treatment, they'll open up to me... and they'll stop seeing me as some northern stranger, let alone enemy.

There's one thing that makes me feel at home: The cold air, the gray skies... Yearfall here is not too different from a day in the Summits, though I miss the snow.

- Helên

3705.title: In Sickness And In Health
3705.text:
Yolanda is still weak. 

She can barely lift her body from the bed... She sleeps, has hot and cold flashes at night. I muffle her pained grunts with the pillow. We can't let them know we're here. 

They're always out there, prowling, shrieking through the night. We're surrounded. I don't want them to be our end... I want peace. I'll be by your side forever. I promise. 

I love you, Yolanda. 

— Alienor

3706.title: Captain's Journal, Day Six of Midyear, 512 D.A.
3706.text:
The raiders have besieged us these past two days, attacking from the bridge. Their eyes... such madness... We have withheld so far, but only just. 

We may not survive the next assault. I've ordered to rig the pass with our last munitions. If those Scavengers return, WE ARE PREPARED.

— Captain Arkwright

3707.title: On Elixir Well, The Springs Of The Elixir
3707.text:
Another Elixir Well is built on the backs of workers, slaving away tirelessly to gouge a tunnel into the earth. The plans for this construction are... otherworldly.

The chasm spits fumes with every jab. Thin veils of mist cause headaches and irritate the eyes... at least they haven't caused a lasting sickness yet. 

Such destruction and upheaval... All for "the Elixir". I hope this foul air will not spread to Lone Thistle.
— Balthazar, 498 D.A.

3708.title: Spectacular Progress Is Being Made
3708.text:
To all who set their eyes upon my wonderous —  no, allow me to begin again.

To the people of Meldore, and all of Embervale — I have conquered this terrain with my greatness! I'm afraid that's not right, either... 

The bridge is nearly finished, and I cannot find the words to express my joy, confound it! How lucky we had a bountiful mine so close by for materials and ore! 

One thing I do know: I'll name this bridge Braelyn, after my 5th Aunt! Though I'm not sure she would be flattered... for her and the bridge share not just the name, but a brash nature. 

Signed,
Cade Hawthorn, Yearwake, 490 D.A.

3709.title: Captain's Journal, Day Twenty of Midyear, 512 D.A.
3709.text:
We are hungry. We had to destroy the bridge — and with it our connection to supplies. But it worked: we haven't seen any more "Scavengers". The Cinder Vault — and those within it — are safe, and should remain so. 

If we are to avoid starvation in Yearfall, we may have to take our chances in the horrible Shroud. Either choice is certain death... 

Perhaps my men are right. In whispered words, they speak of the end times — of an end to the Dawn Age, the empire of man... But we must stand tall. There's no way but forward.
— Captain Arkwright

3710.title: An Old Sight, Rediscovered
3710.text:
I never thought I'd see the sunset on this side of the Pillars of Creation again. The eventide was brighter when I was young. A vibrant haze of lavender or grape, a mix of tangerine and marigold, a florid blush before the dark. Now, gray.
I pray the Ancients protect the northern caravan with their glory and light. I put my faith in Commander Cyrus. 
Longkeep is in sight... My people tire, but we cannot rest. We have to push harder for every soul we've lost. Our step must be swift, I learned. 

I have a strange feeling. This... dread. That I won't be able to linger, that I'll walk alone once more... Why can I not shake this fear? No, this... premonition?

— Queen Jezmina of Orindell, on a mellow yearwake's morn in 508 D.A.

3711.title: Metamorphism
3711.text:
Even during times of Shroud and war, there is light. A flicker. A spark of hope.
A group of Ancients spoke to me... younglings, smaller in stature — kinder. Empathetic, rueful... Or perhaps remorseful.

For the first time, in an age of outcries, they hushed. They plan to build "Cinder Vaults", and vessels that will guide an Ancient Flame into a human shell. Body and mind, Flame and flesh... a mortal soul born from fire, able to banish the fog.

Hopefully, we can bring forward a new age this way.
— Balthazar, 506 D.A.

3712.title: Day 1 — Stuck In The Elevator (Again)
3712.text:
The elevator broke. Again.
I told the overseer to issue proper repairs countless times. This is where it got me. Stuck in an elevator, with no one else left on shift.

Last time this happened, the guys were trapped for 2 days, but the shipment they were stuck with contained plenty of food and a sabertooth pelt to sleep on. Seems like I don't share their luck. All I've got is a load of books, parchment, and a creaking wagon to lie on.

At least I won't have to wait long until I'm saved.

3713.title: Fruit Basket Is Empty Again!!
3713.text: The 8 and a half bell peppers we're allotted every two weeks don't cut it. Are bell peppers even fruits?

3714.title: Day 2 — Where is everybody?
3714.text:
Someone should've come by, but the outpost is empty. No one answers my calls for help. Even worse, I think I hear something shuffling beneath me. At first, I felt it was the bandits from the south port again but the noises didn't sound human.

Come to think of it, the overseer mentioned something about the rising Shroud. Maybe they shut down the site until further notice? It's no use. I'll have to rescue myself!

I moved one of the carts to the platform's edge and stockpiled the cargo there. It wasn't quite high enough to climb out, so I started stacking loose books on top. I'm rapidly losing sunlight, so I won't try to climb out now. Scaling this unstable construction is dangerous enough, even without the encroaching darkness.

3715.title: Nomad's Drop Trade Outpost — Rules:
3715.text:
Remember our three rules for workplace safety and productivity:

1. Follow the schedule!
2. Lift with your legs, not your back! Support each other with heavy cargo!
3. In case of elevator malfunction, report to the shift overseer!

(The fine print reads: If you're early, you're on time. If you're on time, you're late. If you're late, you're fired. No paid overtime. Fruit basket refilled biweekly.)

3716.title: Keep This Between Us!
3716.text:
I was surprised to see Willie so "protective" over those color pots we got from Nomad's Drop. I've never known him to be an artist — unless you want to call all his fingerpainting "art"...

Well, they're not worth much, so there's no point in holding on to them. We might as well pull a little prank on Willie then!

I grabbed some of those precious parcels from the last haul and put 'em up top.
Maybe that'll keep Willie away from fingerpainting and refocus him on being a cold-blooded robber unafraid to shank, steal, and smuggle.

3765.title: In A World Destined for Ruin
3765.text:
Humanity will fade, as all beings do. Their light will flicker and die, untouched by the eternal Flame. 

Meaningless and minuscule in the face of near-endless insight, burning brightly. 

Turning to dust as we turn to fire. An endless cycle of ruin and turmoil.

3766.title: Tired
3766.text:
We would pretend to read them as children... But now, the obelisks hide their truths.

I was a fool to think I could find salvation here. No one hears my prayers, and I feel so tired. I wish you were by my side, brother. 

Eternity beckons...

Forgive me.
— Vettel

3767.title: My Final Journey
3767.text:
My brother, all hope seems lost for me. The nurse, Helên, says there's nothing for me to do but rest... But I won't have it. 

The people of the Kindlewastes speak of the Ancients as if they're all-mighty. Do you recall the obelisk? That Ancient monument that captured our childish minds so, so long ago? 

I will make my way there, no matter what. 
Perhaps there's a cure for me yet. Do not follow — you can't stop me. 

— Vettel

3768.title: The Church Was Destroyed!
3768.text:
Curses! Last night's wind made a mess of our church — or what was left of it. Everett was right. We should have reinforced the roof when we still had the chance. He'll relish that, too! 

Now I must patch the holes, but I can't recall where I had last placed the chest with the materials... I thought I saw it near the church, but I can't find it anywhere! Did my eyes grow tired with age after all?

3769.title: A New Season, Yearwake, 507 D.A.
3769.text:
The new arrivals have wasted no time breaking ground, building something. A Flame Sanctum, Salim says. Their determination to the Ancients and the Flame is... fanatical. To think that we were all one people just about 25 years ago astounds me. 

Some nights I've lingered near the caravan. Salim insists. Over the fire, they talk of their home, the sands, and the creeping ruin. I can't understand their devotion, but I feel their sorrow. Everyone bleeds the same, as I've said... 

Salim says I am like a daffodil, the first sign of yearwake. He is a fool... though a sweet one.

- Helên

3770.title: A Refuge, Yearfall, 506 D.A.
3770.text:
A small caravan of refugees arrived from the Kindlewastes today. And I thought my journey had been long...

I've never spoken with anyone from the Kingdom of Orindell, and the thought made me nervous, but there was no time to tattle. I dove into work, dressing the wounds. A battle for life and death, even now. Sadly, some lost. We put them to rest in the crypt below. May the northern winds guide them to the afterlife.

There's one who might live despite it all. A deep leg wound — but maybe not too far gone. The wounded, Salim, smiles a lot. Says he owes me his life... just luck, I think.

- Helên

3771.title: One Foot in the Grave
3771.text:
We laid another one to rest today. Poor folk. Traveled all this way looking for respite, only to find ruins and scraps. This church won't hold, Helên said as much. The wind howls and forges new paths into our halls every night. 
Storms tore our roof apart, and we're too busy tending to the caravan's people to patch it up. Yet, we must stay. We are needed here and will hardly find shelter elsewhere. 

Burying these vagabonds next to relics and artifacts feels wrong to me, but perhaps Helên is right. Maybe the old times must make way for new customs and rites. Perhaps we may find that spark that united us decades ago once more.

3772.title: The Ancient Spire, Beacons Of Light
3772.text:
These spires stretch to the firmament and deny entry to those who are unworthy. The ancient breed enters, but I never see them leave... I've 2 theories: 
1. The Ancient Spires are somehow connected to another, and the silent ones travel between them as they please. 
2. The Ancient Spires serve as a burial site, similar to the Flame Shrines. The Ancients store all knowledge of the land in the Flame here when they leave the mortal plane.

One way or another, I cannot enter. When I step on the ornate plate, nothing occurs. What a shame.
— Balthazar, 507 D.A.

3773.title: Venture Forth
3773.text:
It's done. The Cinder Vessel is a delicate contraption, still volatile, yet brimming with potential and hope. The first human to enter will be our true prototype, the kindling of a new spark.

Thankfully, the Blacksmith volunteered. He must enter the vessel... and sleep until roused anew, lest he slips into eternity. 

May the ashes of one age sustain the seeds of the next.

Balthazar, 508 D.A.

3774.title: Eureka!
3774.text:
By the Ancients, I've done it! Equilibrium. The subject sleeps, yet can be awakened. They are dead, yet alive! The subject does not decay — is untouched by the coarse flow of time. A Flame's soul in a mortal body — Igni serves as proof!
We can survive! We can endure. These Cinder Vessels will be our only chance amidst the Shroud. We have no other choice.

Balthazar, 507 D.A.

3775.title: Another Failure
3775.text:
The Cinder Vessel broke down during testing. The coalescent flame charred the rat inside. A bright flash, then, nothing. Thankfully, the side effect of blindness was only temporary.

I've acquired a new subject. Another rat, Igni. Hopefully, our path to salvation. I cannot accept more setbacks. I will ensure that the Cinder Vessel holds as if my life depended on it. It may well.

Balthazar, 506 D.A.

3776.title: Imagine This:
3776.text:
You spot sunken stone pillars on the horizon, obscured by mounds of dirt. They stretch towards the sky like a titan's stone-cold fingerbones. The mark of a hidden tomb! The stairs inside lead into darkness. Torch in hand, you slip down into uncertainty. Into dread. Yet, your search drives you deeper. A morbid treasure calls for you, left to rot in the dust! Is it family jewels? Heirlooms from faraway shores? Whatever it is, my friend, it'll be the foundation of our empire! The cornerstone to a fortress raised from spilled blood!

Sound good? I know the rough location. If you take up the search, Gerith, I'll split the goods. Deal?

3777.title: Blood Before Wisdom
3777.text:
Our Scholar of the Empyrean is fading.
He walks slower now, can't make his rounds to the Night Sanctums like before. He's been our guide for decades—and for decades, we've made these offerings. But lately, doubt grows among us.
The Ancients have not returned. Not in many years. 
Their absence once felt sacred. Now, it feels like abandonment.

And today, left by the Ancients and burdened to make the choice alone, the Scholar named his successor.
His own son.

The announcement came without ceremony, without counsel—just a decree passed from fading lips.
But we've barely seen the boy. He's no elder. He's never stepped inside the Sanctums alone.

Some bowed their heads, still clinging to old reverence. But more kept their heads high—eyes filled with doubt.

Is this how it ends?
I fear the Ancients won't bless us with their presence again.

3778.title: Day 3
3778.text:
Stupid, damnable books
Who even reads books anymore
This can't be real

I tried climbing out at the crack of dawn, but I fell off the darn stack

Fall was bad

Shoulder is aching, head is ringing
Even worse, the wagon is broken

If the overseer sees this, I can kiss my position goodbye

Trying again tomorrow
Or whenever I wake up
I have to lie down
Everything spins

3779.title: Day 4?
3779.text:
Don't know how long I slept. In my dreams, I saw velvety, blue waves while voices serenaded me to join them in the deep. Weird dream. Must be because I hit my head in the fall. Yelling for help. I'm starving. Ate paper. Stomach hurts. Can't feel my arm.

Day 5
My voice is gone. Throat feels like it's closing up. 
Something tastes rotten
Can't tell if it's the paper or my tongue

Day 6
Tried climbing out again. Fell. Hands blistered. 
The sun burns me. The voices cry.
For a moment I thought the elevator was moving
My head spins

Day
What day is today
I don't know 
Still hungry
I long to eat flesh

??
It's in the air
All around me
The voices, the rot
There's no escape
There's no air 
I'm sinking forever

3780.title: Smoke On The Horizon
3780.text:
A blazing fire dances atop the roofs of Surat's Rest. We were too late. 

They came from Raven's Keep — escaped inmates, with a penchant for fire. Now, our esteemed town is a pyre of madness. I tremble at the sight. What would mother do? 

She'd move before the sun rose, crown held high. Leave all baggage behind — swift and silent, carried by the wind. The road to Long Keep is a treacherous one... We must make haste.
Glory to Queen Pikemead. Bless the Ancients. 
— Jezmina, 507 D.A.

3781.title: There's Nothing Here!!
3781.text:
You'd think queen Jezmina would travel with style — some class, yes? Some luxury? Some Elixir, right? NOTHING! Just... paints and pillows— pah! 

At least I found an Almanac of Plants and Seedlings in Jezmina's tent. I'll just pretend as though there wasn't any other loot if Simon asks. Hope I can fool him... keen-eyed, that guy.

Other than my private little treasures,  there's barely anything for Surat's Rest... except the dried Yucca Fruit, maybe. Don't tell matron Kendal! They're mine, too!

3782.title: To My Beloved Queen,
3782.text:
Your skin, tinted olive brown, stunning and soft... Your voice — a roar, a hush — always a sweet sonnet on your lips. My heart blossoms at the sight of you. I want to walk alongside you, to see your footsteps next to mine in the sand... to feel the desert wind, and to dance with you in my arms... It's all I hope for. 

— Emily

3783.title: He Knows Too Much
3783.text:
1... 2... 3... 4... 
It's not working! Counting does not calm me down. I'm furious.
I am the Scholar of this village. It's my duty to collect the letters, the books, any offerings people wish to leave in the Night Sanctums. But Garrick... every single time I come by he hands me a stack of letters. I know he is a true believer—desperate for the goodwill of the Ancients.
I also know it's strictly forbidden to open the letters entrusted to me.
But I'm only human — and today I gave in.
And guess what I found?
Garrick has been spilling everything to the Ancients! Every little whisper he hears, every private moment he's not supposed to witness. And now comes the best part: he wrote that I have been cheating on my wife. 

Yes, it's true. 
I know it's wrong, but HOW DARE HE write it down? What if that letter had fallen into the wrong hands? 
Unbelievable. I need to take care of this...

3784.title: Costner Meyers's Powerful Elixir
3784.text:
Attention, weary travelers! Do not heed the violent rumors surrounding this land. Beneath the very ground lies a cure-all for what ails you! As the new owner of this land I, Costner Meyers, kindly invite you to sample my "Incredible Elixir" — which came to me in a miraculous vision!

Anyone who comes by before the end of yearfall will get the first flask for half the prize!

Try it, and you will find yourself transformed! Come one, come all!

— Costner Meyers

3785.title: The Albaneve Summits
3785.text:
Location: Embervale (North East)

Climate: Alpine
Precipitation: From 500 mm (leeward) to 2000 mm (windward)

Flora & Fauna:
The frigid summits are defined by low to sub-zero temperatures, which cover the local peaks in thick layers of snow. Below the frost, only a few species dare to thrive. Yaks have proven resilient to the climate due to their insulating coat of fur. Their biggest adversary is not the cold, but the Cyclops that roam the bluffs looking for a feast to roast.

Geological & Mineral Data 
Many rare earths and minerals can be found in the mountains. Red marble, amethyst, and even ancient deposits of obsidian hide deep within the rock. 

Summary: 
The freezing cold of the summits is considered unpleasant, if not hostile, by most lifeforms (especially ours!) Still, between snow-covered fields and the aurora borealis dancing above, life persists.

3786.title: Code Violet
3786.text:
I declare that my work on your new alarm system is hereby concluded. I consider Violet V2 a notable improvement over the previous iteration! Please find the key data concerning the functionality below.

Most established features were kept: When an intruder is spotted, code violet is triggered, and the facility will lock down. As before, the system is connected to the pressure plates embedded in the floor. Should they detect unauthorized personnel, they will sound the alarm.

Additionally, however, we've been granted a set of Signal and Intrusion Reveal Nodes (S.I.R.N.), courtesy of Constantio. These surveillance constructs will alert the system to intruders, should they be spotted in their vicinity. This will awaken the guard units.

Of course, you may recall the last "false" alarm we suffered... alongside the S.P.D.R. malfunction. Sneaking past security gone rogue in an effort not to perish is tedious, isn't it? Well, you're in luck! With Violet V2, I've implemented a fail-safe: A button inside the control room that can turn off the alarm.

Should questions or complications arise, feel free to contact me.

3787.title: The Veilwater Basin
3787.text:
Location: Embervale (North West)

Climate: Tropical, Marine
Precipitation: Around 3000 mm annually

Flora & Fauna:
The Veilwater Basin is characterized by crystal lakes and lush ecological variety. The rivulets teem with fish, and docile species such as the capybara can be encountered enjoying bananas and coconuts by the shore.
Despite this bliss, considerable dangers lurk below the water. The Basin was previously home to the Drak'Dal, a subspecies or tribe of the Drak. Their temples and altars may be no more than flooded ruins, but as a highly territorial species, they may eventually attempt to reclaim their old hunting grounds.

Geological & Mineral Data 
The coastal region is rich with gold, nacre, and pearls. Unfortunatly, many resources are buried beneath the water's surface, requiring eager gatherers to expose themselves to the elements.

Summary: 
The Veilwater Basin may appear like a paradise at first, but its foreboding history may yet reveal a dark future. Nevertheless, the area remains a fascinating botanical playground with an endless amount of genetic material to probe.

3788.title: The Revelwood
3788.text:
Location: Embervale (Mid-West)

Climate: Continental, Humid
Precipitation: Around 1200 mm annually

Flora & Fauna:
This biosphere is rich in a variety of hardwood species and wildlife. The thick underbrush and dense canopy deserve special attention, as they shelter countless insects, and most notably, arachnids.
Alongside the many muddied pathways, strawberries, chamomile, flax, and indigo plants foster a fragrant and colorful environment. Despite this enticing pull of the bosque, it is advised not to wander off the pathways. Boars roam in the forest, aggressively defending their farrowing nests and young.

Geological & Mineral Data 
Alongside the many mossy cliff faces, wanderers are likely to find bright orange deposits of clay, copper, and, at lower levels, amber.

Summary:
